Within a single crystal, Kerr-active regions are optically distinct from their Kerr-silent surroundings in co-registered reflection maps. These observations indicate that carrier self-doping, rather than ideal altermagnetic order alone, governs the giant magneto-optical response, and establish telecom-wavelength Kerr imaging as a practical readout for altermagnetic spintronics.

items.title: Microscopic origin of Boson peak in two-dimensional scalar spring network
items.summary: We proposed a non-analytic model to explain the microscopic origin of the anomalous vibrational density of states (DOS), the Boson peak (BP), in amorphous solids based on the scalar dynamical matrix of a network with springs and nodes. We argue that disorder can be classified into two factors: fluctuation of spring strength and fluctuation of coordination numbers (the number of springs connected to a node). The results suggest that BP originates from fluctuation of coordination numbers, while the fluctuation of spring strength only contributes to the effect of damping and has very limited effect on low frequency DOS. This work converts complexity into simplicity and provides a direct answer to the puzzle of the microscopic origin of BP in amorphous solids.

items.title: Spontaneous duality breaking and the invertibility of non-invertible symmetries
items.summary: Alongside symmetry and topology, duality is used as an organizing principle throughout modern physics. Dualities are, however, often not exact and, consequently, implemented by a non-invertible operator, giving rise to a non-invertible symmetry at self-dual quantum critical points. Considering the specific example of the transverse-field Ising model, an archetype for both (self-)duality and non-invertible symmetry, we show that its duality can be made exact by a local adjustment of the boundary conditions. In the modified model with exact duality, the symmetry emerging at the quantum critical point is invertible. Moreover, we find that the exact duality necessitates the presence of an anomalous edge degree of freedom, thus realizing a duality-based rather than topology-based bulk-boundary correspondence. The exactness of the duality furthermore seems to suggest that the spontaneous breaking of a global symmetry can also be described as the spontaneous breakdown of a local dual symmetry. We show that this apparent contradiction of Elitzur's theorem can be resolved by considering the required symmetry-breaking fields. This moreover leads to the concept of spontaneous duality breaking, in which arbitrarily small interactions with an embedding environment distinguish between mathematically equivalent dual partners, in direct analogy to the spontaneous breakdown of ordinary symmetries. We argue that both duality-based edge modes and spontaneous duality breaking emerge generally across systems in which a local-global duality can be made exact. Together, these phenomena introduce a conceptually novel interplay between duality, symmetry and topology, that is applicable across diverse areas of physics.

items.title: Evaluation of External Magnetic Flux Density in Piezo-Flexomagnetic Nanobeams Using a Hybrid 1D-2D Finite Element Framework
items.summary: Most theoretical models of piezo-flexomagnetic nanostructures forcibly impose magnetic isolation at the structure-air interface, neglecting the external magnetic domain entirely. This mathematical compromise limits the model's capability to account for stray-field behavior in non-contact applications. To overcome this gap, our study proposes a fully coupled hybrid finite element formulation combining a 1D Timoshenko beam model with a 2D magneto-static problem, encompassing both the beam body and the surrounding air domain. By continuously mapping 1D structural kinematics into the 2D space to define the mechanically induced magnetic flux, and subsequently integrating the resulting 2D scalar potential back into 1D static generalized magnetic loads, this framework enhances the capability of the simple 1D beam model. The results present the distribution of an external magnetic flux in piezo-flexomagnetic structures and identify the material parameters driving this. Ultimately, the proposed computational method extends the boundary of a 1D beam model to an infinite-domain multiphysics environment.

items.title: Predicting the conditions for observing the Mpemba effect
authors: Yue Liu, Tan Van Vu, Rapha\"el Ch\'etrite, Fr\'ed\'eric van Wijland, Hisao Hayakawa
items.summary: The Mpemba effect, a counterintuitive phenomenon where a hotter system relaxes faster than a colder one, has been widely observed in various nonequilibrium systems. Despite this progress, the fundamental structural features of the energy landscape required for its emergence remain a subject of debate. In this study, we investigate the conditions for the Mpemba effect within one-dimensional overdamped Langevin dynamics. We classify the potential landscapes based on the presence of single or double wells, their symmetry properties, and the existence of walls. We establish that the existence of the effect is primarily driven by the presence of boundaries, either hard or soft, rather than the specific internal structure of the potential landscape, such as metastability or the number of minima. By employing a spectral decomposition of the Fokker-Planck operator, we analyze the behavior of the first nontrivial eigenmode and demonstrate that its derivative acts as a Dirac delta peak in the low-temperature regime. This helps us elucidate the mechanism underlying the Mpemba effect: it appears as the interplay between this behavior and the initial population dynamics in a non-trivial way induced by the presence of the wall. Our analysis provides a unified classification across single- and double-well potentials, highlighting the crucial role of boundary conditions and asymmetry. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this framework allows for the engineering of potential landscapes capable of producing multistage Mpemba transitions.

items.title: Atomic-scale visualization of the toroidal order in a trimeric Dy(III) single-molecule toroic
authors: Michael J. Jenkins, Madalynn G. Marshall, Jie Xing, Muthu Satheeshkumar, Brandon D. Watson-Sanders, Xiaoping Wang, Christina M. Hoffmann, Gopalan Rajaraman, Huibo Cao, Rongying Jin, Zi-Ling Xue
items.summary: Single-molecule toroics (SMTs) offer a unique platform for next-generation quantum devices utilizing head-to-tail spin alignments in the compounds. Presence of toroidal moments in SMTs has been essentially based on magnetometry and ab initio calculations. Here, we report observation and probe of the toroidal moment in [Dy3(OH)(teaH2)3(paa)3]Cl(OMe) [teaH3: triethanolamine; paaH: N-(2-pyridyl)-acetoacetamide] from mapping of Dy3+ magnetic susceptibility tensors by polarized neutron diffraction (PND). Neutron diffraction under variable magnetic fields demonstrates field-induced magnetization along the c-axis with toroidal moments anti-parallelly stacked, providing definite proof of the toroidal moment. Magnetometry studies confirm the toroidal ground state. For the first time, the combined use of PND, variable-field neutron diffraction, ab initio calculations, and magnetometry is introduced as a robust and quantitative methodology to probe molecular-scale toroidal magnetism. This integrated approach overcomes limitations of earlier indirect methods, establishes a benchmark framework for investigating SMTs, and provides valuable insights for the design of molecular quantum materials.

items.title: Dynamics of repeated BEC formation and extraction in dimple traps
authors: Kyrylo Kovalchuk, Dominik Pfeiffer, Ludwig Lind, Mark Edwards, Alexander Yakimenko, Gerhard Birkl
items.summary: We investigate repeated Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) formation and extraction in a dimple trap embedded in a reservoir of thermal atoms using a kinetic model. The model includes pulsed extraction, evaporation, three-body losses, and thermal-atom replenishment. Three extraction protocols are compared: extraction of all atoms from the dimple (BEC and thermal atoms), full and partial extractions of the BEC, but not of the thermal atoms. Residual atoms in the dimple after extraction seed subsequent Bose-stimulated growth and reduce the recovery time between extractions, but also enhance density-dependent losses. For all protocols, repeated extraction of BECs can be achieved without replenishment, but the number of BEC formations is limited by reservoir depletion and heating. With continuous replenishment, the system can reach a periodic steady-state regime, after an initial transient period, controlled by the externally imposed rates of extraction pulses and thermal-atom input. Within the explored parameter range, partial BEC extraction gives the highest efficiency, particularly for short extraction periods and high input rates. These results identify seeding by residual populations of BECs and thermal atoms as a kinetic mechanism for improving repeated condensate production in dimple traps.

items.title: Nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang dynamics of grain boundaries
items.summary: The kinetic roughening of driven grain boundaries (GBs) is mediated by the collective behavior of disconnections, whose long-range 1/r elastic interactions distinguish them from conventional growing surfaces. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations show that the roughness of driven GBs undergoes a sharp crossover as the applied strain increases, with the Hurst exponent (H) increasing from approximately 0.33 to 0.8. We develop a nonlocal fractional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (fKPZ) theory to describe this low-temperature behavior, where the 1/r nonlocal elasticity behaves as the fractional relaxation of the GB morphology. The results show that the spatially-correlated noise associated with disconnection avalanches interacts with the KPZ nonlinearity to produce the post-crossover roughening observed in atomistic simulations. The post-crossover roughness exponent (H ~ 0.8) is comparable to values reported for dynamic fracture, suggesting the underlying physics shared by the collective behavior of defects (e.g., disconnections, dislocations) and interfacial roughening.

items.title: Statistical mechanics of a three-body Hopfield model with finite connectivity
items.summary: A three-body Hopfield model defined on sparse random graphs with finite mean connectivity is studied using a replica-symmetric (RS) analysis. By extending the functional replica framework for conventional two-body finite-connectivity Hopfield models, self-consistent equations for the local-field distribution are derived and solved numerically by population dynamics. At low memory load, the RS analysis shows a discontinuous transition between paramagnetic and retrieval states, accompanied by coexistence of distinct fixed points and an upper spinodal of the retrieval solution. Starting the RS population dynamics from an uninformative finite-amplitude field distribution also leads to a spin-glass-like (SG-like) fixed point at low temperatures, even though the paramagnetic fixed point remains locally stable. As the number of embedded patterns increases, the retrieval solution disappears, while the SG-like RS solutions are found at high load. However, the local instability and thermodynamic inconsistencies of the low-temperature RS solutions indicate the limitations of the RS description of the glassy regime. Finite-size Monte Carlo simulations using population annealing agree well with the RS description of the retrieval branch during heating but exhibit glassy trapping behavior under cooling. Such trapping can occur even for a single embedded pattern, where conventional cross-talk noise among stored patterns is absent, indicating the importance of sparse connectivity and three-body interaction. The characteristic number of embedded patterns separating different solution regimes grows approximately linearly with the mean connectivity, corresponding to finite characteristic load ratios. These results clarify how sparse connectivity and many-body interactions influence the stability and accessibility of retrieval states in associative memory.

items.title: Statistical properties of quadrangular surfaces
authors: Hrant Topchyan, Rudik Badalyan, Ara Sedrakyan
items.summary: We investigate the statistical properties of random quadrangular surfaces generated by different randomization procedures: the Gruzberg-Kl\"umper-Nuding-Sedrakyan (GKNS) construction, and two newly introduced generalizations of dynamical triangulations (DT), dynamical (DQ) and general quadrangulations (GQ). We formulate these surfaces within a unified graph-theoretic framework and establish the relationships between the elementary operations defining the different ensembles. For GKNS surfaces, we demonstrate that the construction is equivalent to two mutually constrained percolation processes and determine the associated critical point and critical exponents, revealing deviations from ordinary percolation. For DQ and GQ, we analyze the underlying Markov chains and determine the scaling of mixing and relaxation times. We further analyze all three ensembles through their degree distributions, degree correlations, distance statistics, and Hausdorff dimensions. While DQ exhibits exponentially decaying degree distributions and geometric properties similar to DT, GKNS and GQ display broad, scale-free degree distributions. Moreover, GKNS surfaces possess an asymptotic Hausdorff dimension $\Delta_H\approx 2$, whereas DQ and GQ approach $\Delta_H\approx 4$, similarly to DT. This indicates that DQ is compatible with the universal behavior of DT, while GKNS and GQ define distinct classes of random geometry, implying a different underlying measure in the space of random surfaces and a possible geometric framework for a new class of noncritical string theories.

items.title: Non-Hermitian Random Matrix Theory of Jamming in Active Disordered Media
items.summary: We develop a non-Hermitian random-matrix description of active jammed systems in which a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by non-reciprocal Ginibre couplings. Within a Hermitized self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA), we derive a scalar susceptibility equation predicting \(J\sim\alpha_0^{-6/7}\) at the marginal point. Direct random-matrix calculations confirm that the mechanically relevant response is governed by singular values rather than complex eigenvalues. They further reveal strong finite-size fluctuations: near marginality, a large fraction of the total susceptibility is typically carried by the smallest singular value. These results distinguish the smooth large-\(N_c\) SCBA response from the extreme singular-value statistics of finite non-Hermitian systems.

items.title: Local B-site chemistry controls oxygen-vacancy energetics in Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn perovskites for thermochemical hydrogen production
authors: Manish Kumar (Washington University in St. Louis), Natalia Ali (Arizona State University), Matthew D. Witman (Sandia National Laboratories), Shang Zhai (The Ohio State University), James E. Miller (Arizona State University), Ivan Ermanoski (Arizona State University), Ellen B. Stechel (Arizona State University), Robert B. Wexler (Washington University in St. Louis)
items.summary: Two-step thermochemical water splitting driven by concentrated solar heat is a scalable route to renewable hydrogen, but it requires oxides whose oxygen-vacancy formation energies balance facile reduction with favorable reoxidation. Perovskite solid solutions can tune this balance, but the relationship between bulk stoichiometry and local defect energetics remains poorly understood. Here we map oxygen-vacancy formation energetics across Ca-Ce-Ti-Mn (CCTM) perovskites by combining first-principles calculations with a coverage-constrained special quasirandom structure approach that realizes all fifteen symmetry-distinct oxygen nearest-neighbor environments, an interpretable crystal-feature model whose fitted coefficients directly encode the underlying Born-Haber thermochemistry, and a fine-tuned defect graph neural network. Local B-site chemistry dominates the oxygen-vacancy formation energy $E_\mathrm{v}$: varying the nearest-neighbor Mn fraction shifts $E_\mathrm{v}$ by 1.0-1.5 eV depending on local Ce content, whereas A-site Ce variation contributes a smaller, Mn-dependent shift of 0.2-0.6 eV. Short-range B-site cation order, if it can be established and kinetically retained through processing, is therefore a candidate means of tuning redox performance without changing bulk composition. Composition-space maps identify a Ce/Mn-balanced region (~29-33% Ce on the A site and 58-67% Mn on the B site) combining a high fraction of vacancy sites within the targeted $E_\mathrm{v}$ window with phase stability and solubility, whose predicted redox cycle capacity matches or exceeds the ceria benchmark at 1350 $^\circ$C rather than the roughly 1600 $^\circ$C ceria requires. Measurements on three CCTM compositions show cycle capacity increasing monotonically with Ce content under protocols close to the model conditions. The design rules are expected to transfer to related perovskite families.

items.title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
authors: S. Feyrer, V. Dimic, I. Lobato, A. Kirchner, P. Drexler, L. Rupp, D. Bougeard, T. Lindemann, S. Gronin, G. Gardner, M. J. Manfra, G. F. R. Ruiz, C. A. Balseiro, L. Arrachea, M. Aprili, N. Paradiso, C. Strunk, L. Tosi
items.summary: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive probe of anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid systems.

items.title: Fubini-Study Speed and Short-Time Identification of Bosonic Instability
items.summary: We ask what short-time quantum distinguishability reveals about instability in quadratic bosonic systems. For a fixed autonomous quadratic Hamiltonian, the infimum of the Fubini-Study speed over centered pure Gaussian inputs equals the Euclidean norm of the positive real parts of the flow eigenvalues divided by the square root of 2. The infimum is attained exactly when the flow generator is diagonalizable. We also derive the minimum speed under a finite squeezing budget for a detuned parametric amplifier. For a lossy single-mode amplifier with a common phase-insensitive Markovian bath, two return-fidelity traces, from the bare vacuum and a calibrated squeezed vacuum, determine the growth margin, damping, and diffusion from their initial slopes and curvatures. Finite-window simulations illustrate how the traces distinguish cases on opposite sides of the instability threshold.

items.title: Unconventional Pressure Evolution of Spin-Density-Wave State in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$
authors: Xiaoxiang Zhou, Shiyu Xie, Liangxin Qiao, Hengyuan Zhang, Jun Shu, Rui Liu, Mengwu Huo, Deyuan Hu, Hengjie Liu, Chuansheng Hu, Ge He, Zeming Qi, Meng Wang, Dong-Lai Feng, Zengyi Du
items.summary: The discovery of pressure-induced high temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has raised the question of how its spin-density-wave (SDW) state evolves toward the superconducting regime. Here, we report a systematic electronic Raman study of La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51~GPa. Both the SDW gap energy and the transition temperature $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ show an overall increase with pressure, while the dimensionless coupling ratio $2\Delta_{\mathrm{SDW}}/(k_{\mathrm B}T_{\mathrm{SDW}})$ remains approximately pressure independent, indicating a robust strong-coupling character of SDW state. At the same time, the SDW-related Raman peak broadens as pressure is applied, indicating the enhanced damping of the associated electronic excitation. These results reveal an unusual pressure evolution in which the SDW energy scale is enhanced while the SDW state becomes progressively less coherent, providing spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations relevant to superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

items.title: Exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size
items.summary: We present exact expressions of correlation functions between two spins in the boundary row of the two-dimensional rectangular Ising model with periodic-free boundary conditions and finite size. Some properties of exact expressions obtained are discussed. The fundamental property of the Ising model that the long range order emerge as the temperature decrease is shown clearly; expressions of the correlation functions in the thermodynamic limit varies depending on the order of taking limits of two parameters L and N; the impact of different sizes on correlation functions is illustrated with the aid of diagrams. Expressions of the correlation function discussed in this paper in the thermodynamic limit has been presented by previous researchers, and we prove that expressions obtained in this article is identical in form to expressions provided by previous researchers in the thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Topologically protected zero-reflection nodes for perfect crossed Andreev reflection
items.summary: Generating non-locally entangled electron pairs via Cooper-pair splitting is vital for solid-state quantum information processing. However, isolating the underlying crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is challenging due to competing transport processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR). Here, we propose a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction that achieves deterministic, 100\% efficient CAR. We demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($\phi=\pi$), exact destructive Aharonov-Bohm and Peierls interferences structurally forbid ET and AR, respectively. By tuning the central junction hopping, electron reflection is also suppressed to zero. Using the Cauchy argument principle, we prove that this zero-reflection node is topologically protected by a quantized winding number in parameter space. When combined with the precise spatial symmetries of the junction, this exact suppression guarantees a unit CAR probability. We establish that this regime is characterized by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise, providing an unambiguous experimental signature of Cooper-pair splitting. Furthermore, this perfect CAR is nearly broadband within the superconducting gap. While generic structural disorder breaks the spatial symmetries required for the exact cancellation of ET and AR, the crossed Andreev reflection--though no longer perfectly quantized --remains highly dominant under weak disorder, offering a resilient architecture for deterministic nonlocal entanglement generation.

items.title: de Almeida-Thouless Stability and Replica Symmetry Breaking in a Hybrid Watermarking Model with Image and Message Decoding
authors: Tatsuya Uezu, Kao Hayashi, Masaki Kawamura
items.summary: We investigate the de Almeida-Thouless (AT) stability of the replica symmetric (RS) solution for a spread-spectrum watermarking model incorporating Bayes-estimation-based image restoration. In our previously proposed model [1], which simultaneously performs message decoding and image restoration under Gaussian channel noise, a discrepancy between the theoretical predictions of the RS solution and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations was observed in specific parameter regimes. In this paper, by analyzing the blind case where both the original message and image are unknown, we explicitly derive the conditions for the AT stability of the RS solution by clarifying the structure of the replicon eigenspace for the hybrid system. Our results reveal that AT stability is broken precisely in the parameter region where the RS solution deviates from MCMC simulations, thereby successfully explaining the mechanism underlying this discrepancy in terms of replica symmetry breaking (RSB). [1] M. Kawamura, T. Uezu, K. Hayashi, and M. Okada, ``Statistical mechanical evaluation of a spread-spectrum watermarking model with image restoration,'' Phys. Rev. E \textbf{99}, 062132 (2019).

items.title: Trajectory Statistics Govern Mechanical Power Transfer in Active Baths
authors: Chul-Ung Woo, Jiwon Choi, Heiko Rieger
items.summary: In active media, a moving passive object can experience negative drag and receive positive mechanical power from the bath, in contrast to the dissipative response in equilibrium. For a probe moving at velocity $\mathbf{V}$ and interacting weakly with an ideal active bath, we show that free-particle trajectory statistics determine the density response and the resulting bath force. The probe--particle interaction sets the wave-vector weighting, while the imposed motion selects frequencies $\omega_{\mathbf q}=\mathbf q\cdot \mathbf V$, separating bath dynamics from probe properties. The sign of the response spectrum yields probe-independent constraints for mechanical power transfer. Applying this framework to representative active-particle models reveals distinct power-transfer behavior despite identical displacement variances. For prescribed probe motion, the relation predicts drag reversal, motion-induced density distortions, and velocity-dependent friction, in quantitative agreement with simulations. Beyond the mean force, the free-particle trajectory statistics also determine the force autocorrelation. These results provide a route to predict the mechanical response of probes from single-particle trajectory statistics measured in the absence of the probe.

items.title: 10 kV $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
authors: Imteaz Rahaman, Hunter Ellis, Afrouz Taherian, Seyedeh Shadi Mirmohammadi, Botong Li, Berardi Sensale Rodriguez, Michael A. Scarpulla, Kai Fu
items.summary: $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. The ON/OFF ratio increases with optical power density but exhibits a nonmonotonic bias dependence, reaching approximately 15-16 near 5-7 kV. At 10 kV, increased OFF-state conduction and non-ideal transient behavior reduce the switching contrast. These results demonstrate near-infrared photoconductive switching but also highlight critical trade-offs in photoconductive thresholds for impurity states.

items.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
items.summary: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

items.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
authors: Chongzhou Wang, Zhengda Jing, Weichao Yu
items.summary: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/{\pi} phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.

items.title: Devitrification: crystal nucleation and growth mechanisms in glasses
items.summary: If a liquid is cooled rapidly, it may fall out of equilibrium before it can crystallize. It may, however, crystallize later from the nonequilibrium glassy state. Using the Random First-Order Transition (RFOT) theory of glasses, we discuss a variety of mechanisms of crystallization as a route to devitrification. Ordinary nucleation is sped up by the frozen in energy of the glass relative to the liquid. At sufficiently low temperatures, a mechanism of nanonucleation appears, producing nanometer scale crystal inclusions in the glass. Nanocrystallization depends strongly on the local fluctuations in stability, and the transition from classical nucleation and growth to nanocrystallization occurs dominantly through rare, less stable glassy regions that percolate through space, producing an additional dramatic speedup in the crystal nucleation and growth rates. Similar fluctuations in local stability also explain anomalies of crystal growth in deeply supercooled systems.

items.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
authors: Hari Bhandari, Kevin Allen, Kuan-Sen Lin, Yuan Fang,  Arushi, Karthik Rao, Mounica Mahankali, Sanu Mishra, Jian-Xin Zhu, Christopher Lane, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan
items.summary: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathit{\Gamma}\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

items.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
authors: Siyuan Cheng, Yuee Xie, Xiaosen Yang, Yuanping Chen
items.summary: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $\pi$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.

items.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
items.summary: The zero-point energy of an $LC$ circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this fluctuation is the bulk quantum weight $K_{\rm bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge have squared dipole matrix elements that sum to an edge weight $K_{\rm edge}\ge |C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. At weak coupling, which a growing flake eventually leaves, a circuit slower than the edge modes reads $K_{\rm bulk}+K_{\rm edge}$, averaged over two field directions, and a faster one approaches $K_{\rm bulk}$, so the reading depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. In exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes with $|C|=1$ and 2 the summed circular dichroism of the edge sector extrapolates to $|C|$ in magnitude, so that the floor is $|C|$. Above the floor, each edge channel adds a number fixed by the boundary shape and its edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes with one channel follow to within 0.003, while the circular dichroism counts only the net chirality. The avoided crossing of the circuit with the edge mode gives the edge weight in units of the Hall conductance quantum, up to a geometric factor of the capacitor.

items.title: Thermality from a Rindler quench
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Ultracold fermionic atoms in an optical lattice, with a sudden position-dependent change (a quench) in the effective dispersion relation, have been proposed by Rodr\'iguez-Laguna et al. as an analogue spacetime test of the Unruh effect. We provide new support for this analogue by analysing a massless scalar field on a $(1+1)$-dimensional continuum spacetime with a similar quench: an early time Minkowski region is joined at a constant time surface, representing the quench, to a late time static region in which left and right asymptotically Rindler domains are connected by a smooth negative curvature bridge. We show that the quench is energetically mild, and late time static observers, modelled as a derivative-coupling Unruh-DeWitt detector, see thermality, in a temperature that equals the Unruh temperature for observers in the asymptotic Rindler domains. The Unruh effect hence prevails, despite the energy injected into the field by the quench and despite the absence of a late time Killing horizon. These results strengthen the motivation to realise the experimental proposal.

items.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
authors: Varun Menon, Andi Gu, Ramis Movassagh
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

items.title: Interface Energy and Phase Transformations: A Comparative Analysis of Cahn-Hilliard and CALPHAD-based Models in Ternary Substitutional Alloys
authors: Wolfgang Flachberger, Thomas Antretter, Swaroop Gaddikere-Nagaraja, Silvia Leitner, Manuel Petersmann, Jiri Svoboda
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Diffusional phase transformations in alloys are modeled either by phase-field methods of Cahn-Hilliard type, in which a double-well free energy and a gradient term impose an interface energy, or by reactive diffusion models, in which the driving forces follow from the CALPHAD methodology, the convex hull of the molar free energy, and the interface carries no energy. Their numerical schemes are tied to their free energies: phase-field schemes break down when the interface energy is set to zero, and reactive diffusion codes rely on finite differences. We derive, from the thermodynamic extremal principle, a single finite element scheme that covers both limits: the stationarity of the Rayleighian functional (free energy rate plus one half of the dissipation, with mass conservation imposed by multipliers) with respect to the rates, fluxes and multipliers at a frozen state. Fluxes and chemical affinities are primary unknowns, so no derivative of the affinity is required. The time-discrete scheme is the corresponding incremental minimization; it conserves mass exactly and satisfies a discrete energy-dissipation inequality for every convex molar free energy, including the convex hull without regularization. We make explicit that this last case is a degenerate parabolic problem of Stefan type, whose degeneracy can be removed, without altering the free energy, only by a moving mesh; since our aim is the coupling to continuum mechanics and damage on a fixed mesh, we operate at the boundary of degeneracy and show that mass conservation, the energy balance and the second law remain intact there. Thermodynamic consistency is proved for multi-component systems, a scheme relating Onsager and diffusion coefficients is proposed, and the role of interface energy is studied in binary and ternary examples, the latter with vacancies as a non-conserved component.

items.title: Learning to stabilize nonequilibrium phases of matter with active feedback using partial information
authors: Giovanni Cemin, Markus Schmitt, Marin Bukov
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Recent advances in quantum computing experiments have enabled new pathways for feedback control. Here, we investigate the role of information in interactive quantum many-body dynamics to engineer out-of-equilibrium phases of matter. To this end, we train reinforcement learning agents to prevent entanglement spreading in (1+1)-dimensional stabilizer circuits with up to 128 qubits. We find that, above an information threshold, agents learn stochastic near-optimal strategies that prevent the system from reaching volume-law entangled states and instead stabilize area-law scaling. These strategies rely on bottlenecks that divide the system and cap the entanglement in the steady state. Crucially, learned strategies are inherently out of equilibrium, require real-time active feedback, and could not be reproduced by simple human-designed control rules. This work establishes the foundations for information-driven individual control of many interacting quantum degrees of freedom, demonstrating the capabilities of reinforcement learning to stabilize and uncover novel critical properties of many-body nonequilibrium steady states.

items.title: Ultrafast Optical Probing of Laser Processing
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Laser treatment has emerged into a cornerstone of industrial manufacturing. This creates the demand to understand in detail the involved physical processes and their dynamics, to control the process, and to keep guard in-situ the laser manufacturing steps. Given the contactless interaction of light with matter, particularly optical methods appear most suitable for probing laser processing. This chapter reviews the current scientific and technological state of analyzing laser-based material processing by short and ultrashort optical pulses. For that, sequential passive interrogation of material properties (via reflection, absorption, scattering, diffraction, interference, or specific nonlinear responses) can be employed through so-called pump-probe techniques (where the time-resolution is not given by the detector response time but by the duration of an electromagnetic probe pulse that is interrogating the transient scenery at a controlled delay (typ. fs to \mu s) with respect to the arrival of the pump laser pulse). These approaches are capable to analyze on microscopic to macroscopic scales a plethora of different processes involved in laser processing, such as heating, melting, ablation, plasma- and shockwave-formation, optical breakdown in surrounding liquids and gases, shielding and accumulation effects, surface solidification and restructuring, etc. A special focus is set on the variety of ultrafast optical imaging schemes for visualizing the dynamics of laser processing at the surface and in the bulk of the irradiated materials, including photography and microscopy, holography, tomography, ptychography, and coherent diffractive imaging. The chapter provides a historic survey, highlights important scientific and technological developments and breakthroughs, discusses selected applications, explores the requirements and current limitations, and sheds light on emerging future trends.

items.title: Hybridized-Mode Parametric Amplifier in Kinetic-Inductance Circuits
authors: Danial Davoudi, Abdul Mohamed, Shabir Barzanjeh
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Parametric amplification is essential for quantum measurement, enabling the amplification of weak microwave signals with minimal added noise. While Josephson-junction-based amplifiers have become standard in superconducting quantum circuits, their magnetic sensitivity, limited saturation power, and sub-kelvin operating requirements motivate the development of alternative nonlinear platforms. Here we demonstrate a two-mode kinetic-inductance parametric amplifier based on a pair of capacitively coupled Kerr-nonlinear resonators fabricated from NbTiN and NbN thin films. The distributed Kerr nonlinearity of these materials enables nondegenerate four-wave-mixing amplification with gains approaching 40 dB, gain-bandwidth products up to 6.9 MHz, and 1-dB compression powers two to three orders of magnitude higher than those of state-of-the-art Josephson amplifiers. A coupled-mode theoretical model accurately captures the pump-induced modification of the hybridized modes and quantitatively reproduces the observed signal and idler responses. The NbN device exhibits a significantly larger Kerr coefficient and superior gain-bandwidth performance, highlighting the advantages of high-kinetic-inductance materials. Our results establish coupled kinetic-inductance resonators as a robust platform for broadband, high-power, and magnetically resilient quantum-limited amplification, offering a scalable route for advanced readout in superconducting qubits, spin ensembles, quantum dots, and other microwave-quantum technologies.

items.title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
authors: Niamh O'Neill, Benjamin X. Shi, William C. Witt, Blake I. Armstrong, Asmita Niyogi, William J. Baldwin, Paolo Raiteri, Christoph Schran, Angelos Michaelides, Julian D. Gale
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behaviour of CaCO$_3$ in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO$_3$ with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the ''gold-standard'' coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO$_3$ ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

items.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
authors: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford
items.summary: -cross Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.

items.title: Weak ergodicity breaking captured from short-time dynamcis and graph theory
authors: Heiko Georg Menzler, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.

items.title: The Interplay of Data Structure and Imbalance in the Learning Dynamics of Diffusion Models
authors: Flavio Nicoletti, Chenxiao Ma, Enrico Ventura, Luca Saglietti, Stefano Sarao Mannelli
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Real-world datasets are inherently heterogeneous, yet how per-class structural differences and sampling imbalance shape the training dynamics of diffusion models---and potentially exacerbate disparities---remains poorly understood. While models typically transition from an initial phase of generalization to memorizing the training set, existing theory assumes homogeneous data, leaving open how class imbalance and heterogeneity reshape these dynamics. In this work, we develop a high-dimensional analytical framework to study class-dependent learning in score-based diffusion models. Analyzing a random-features model trained on Gaussian mixtures, we derive the feature-covariance spectrum to characterize per-class generalization and memorization times. We reveal the explicit hierarchy governing these dynamics: class variance is the primary determinant of learning order---consistently favoring higher-variance classes---while centroid geometry and sampling imbalance play secondary roles. Specifically, sampling imbalance acts as a modulator that can reverse this ordering and, under strong imbalance, forces minority classes to acquire distinct, delayed inference times during backward diffusion. Together, these results suggest that diffusion models can memorize some classes while others remain insufficiently learned. We validate our theoretical predictions empirically using U-Net models trained on Fashion MNIST.

items.title: Identifiability and endpoint reconstruction of time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from projective trajectory jets
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study the identifiability of smooth time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from phase-resolved Schrodinger trajectories. When the initial state is localized at a chain endpoint, we prove that the projective trajectory jet through order M+1 uniquely determines the first M couplings, their logarithmic time derivatives, and the associated diagonal energy differences at preparation. This derivative order is necessary in the unrestricted real-Jacobi class. If only the first K projective coordinates are observed, even their full Taylor jets leave every deeper instantaneous layer undetermined. We also construct evolutions that are indistinguishable on an observation window separated from preparation but have different endpoint coupling scales and rates. We identify two ways to restore local identifiability: first-order projective and reference-population data at generic times, or second-order data from ceil(M/2) suitable site preparations for independent coupling rates. Statistical distinguishability bounds and finite-window simulations quantify the effects of noise, nuisance coefficients, and acquisition design.

items.title: An Asymptotic Theory of Chain-of-Thought in In-Context Learning
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has become a widely used mechanism for eliciting multi-step reasoning in large language models by generating intermediate reasoning steps at inference time. Yet the scaling behavior of generalization with CoT depth remains poorly understood. To address this question, we study a theoretically solvable model of CoT for in-context weight prediction in linear regression, where test-time reasoning is represented as an iterative refinement of the weight-parameter estimate. Using tools from random matrix theory under high-dimensional asymptotics, we derive an exact formula for the generalization error as a function of reasoning depth, pretraining data amount, and context length. Our analysis reveals a sharp phase transition separating exponential and polynomial improvement, saturation, and overthinking, and characterizes how the optimal reasoning depth scales. We further show that deeper reasoning is most effective with sufficiently rich pretraining and in-context information, whereas limited pretraining or context makes longer reasoning prone to error amplification or saturation. We also validate these predictions through experiments on fully learned linear attention and softmax attention models. Our results provide a unified theoretical account of how test-time CoT depth affects generalization.

items.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.

items.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
authors: Xuan Zhao, Qiuze Sun, Yi Wang, Jin Hu
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

items.title: Hydrogen-Bond Donor-Acceptor Imbalance in Low-Frequency Terahertz Water Spectra
authors: Lilian Najm Alsayed, Florian Pabst, Giuseppe Cassone, Ali Hassanali, Fabio Novelli
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The low-frequency dielectric response of liquid water is commonly described by a dominant Debye relaxation together with additional faster contributions whose microscopic origin remains debated. Here we show that the dielectric function of water between 0.14 and 1.21 THz can be represented by a collective Debye relaxation plus a Drude-Smith term constrained to the zero-dc-conductivity limit. The Drude-Smith spectral weight increases upon heating pure H2O from 20 C to 50 C and decreases upon isotopic substitution (D2O at 20 C vs. H2O at 20 C). Molecular dynamics simulations including nuclear quantum effects show correlated changes in the population of water molecules with unequal numbers of donated and accepted hydrogen-bonds. Ab-initio-based spectra calculations further indicate that the ~0.1-1 THz response contains both nuclear-motion and explicit electronic-polarisation/charge-redistribution contributions. We therefore interpret the excess low-frequency THz response as a localised, mixed nuclear-electronic dielectric response correlated with transient donor-acceptor imbalance in the hydrogen-bond network.

items.title: High-purity entanglement mediated by magnons despite weak coupling
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Entangling distant spins via a shared magnonic bus typically faces a tradeoff: stronger spin-magnon coupling increases the entanglement fidelity, but also the spin decay rate. We propose a protocol that breaks this tradeoff. The magnons couple only to a transition outside the computational basis, in which the Bell state is created. Our protocol is probabilistic, and weak coupling reduces the success probability but not the fidelity. We analyze a setup where the spins are two nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near a magnetic wire. In the absence of NV dephasing, the protocol reaches unit fidelity with a maximally entangled state, for arbitrarily weak coupling. In our simulations via the Monte-Carlo wavefunction approach, the NV-magnon coupling is taken to be one-third of the magnon linewidth. Considering finite NV dephasing, we predict a fidelity of >0.99 for a state-of-the-art rate, and an optimal fidelity of 0.91 for a moderate rate, both at 0.6% success probability.

items.title: Multiphysics simulation of all-optical switching and sequential magneto-optic readout in an integrated Si$_3$N$_4$/GdFeCo waveguide
authors: Muhammad Arief Mulyana, Budi Adiperdana, Ayi Bahtiar
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Femtosecond pulses guided in a silicon nitride waveguide have recently switched a Co/Gd magnetic element patterned on top of it, a step towards magnetic memory built into photonic circuits. The guided mode heats such an element non-uniformly, and, to our knowledge, no calculation has yet followed the written state from this heating to an optical readout. Here we model both steps for an 8 nm GdFeCo film inserted across a Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguide. A three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain calculation gives the absorbed pump energy. This energy drives a four-temperature model and calibrated stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch dynamics, and a later probe pulse reads the recovered state. At the reference fluence, a single pump pulse reverses 86% of the film from either saturated state, and this fraction changes little over a 2.4-fold range of incident fluence. The unswitched cells lie where the absorbed fluence stays below the single-cell threshold, and a threshold rule applied to the absorption map reproduces the full calculation. When the film starts from zero magnetization, thermal noise sets the direction of each recovered local moment at random. Between the saturated and random states, the probe energy fractions change by at most 0.02. The magnetic Faraday and Kerr rotations are far more sensitive and become about 12 and 130 times smaller, respectively, in the random state than in a saturated film. The reflected signal also contains a magnetization-independent geometric background, which can be removed by subtracting a reference signal. The model therefore predicts that a guided probe can distinguish the written states through its polarization. It assumes a homogeneous film and omits heat flow and exchange between neighbouring cells.

items.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Let $Z_N$ be the partition function of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta>1$. Replica theory (Kondor near the critical temperature, Parisi and Rizzo at all temperatures) predicts that the probability that $N^{-1}\log Z_N$ exceeds its typical value by $\delta$ decays like $\exp(-Na\delta^{6/5})$ with an explicit $a$; Aronow and Lopatto recently proved bounds of this order. The exponent is the Legendre transform of the Parisi problem constrained to carry an atom $\theta$ at zero. We show that the constrained minimum exceeds the equilibrium free energy by $c_\beta\theta^5(1+o(1))$, where $c_\beta=\frac{9}{640}\beta^3\rho_\beta(0)^{-3}$ and $\rho_\beta(0)>0$ is the density at zero of the Parisi measure. With the fractional-moment formula this gives the exponent $\frac56(6c_\beta)^{-1/5}\delta^{6/5}(1+o(1))$ as $N\to\infty$ and then $\delta\to0$. The constrained minimizer has a marginal first positive contact, to leading order at $3\theta/(2\rho_\beta(0))$ with an atom $\theta/2$. This plateau calculus applies to every mixture with $\xi'''(0)=0$ whose Parisi measure accumulates at zero; a small field $h$ opens a gap of order $|h|^{2/3}$, and an atom of the Parisi measure at zero, present in every pure $p$-spin model with $p\ge3$, makes the rate leave zero linearly. Near criticality the constant tends to Kondor's value $9/5120$ and the marginal regime ends at a de Almeida-Thouless threshold. For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every $\beta>1$, a finite-step curvature inequality from an unrefereed preprint shows that every constrained minimizer either has an interval of positive contacts, all marginal, or has exactly two atoms, and that the marginal regime ends at a unique de Almeida-Thouless threshold $\theta_c(\beta)$. The laws at every $\beta>1$ use that the Parisi measure accumulates at zero, a theorem of Lopatto also proved in earlier work of the author.

items.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Monodromy line defects arise as boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, providing a natural route to conformal defects with implications in condensed matter, gauge theories and quantum information. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we realize monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $Z_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), the $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $\pi$-twist and reflection). For each defect we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the critical bulk. Among the resolved low-lying defect primaries we find no relevant scalar perturbation preserving all symmetries of the corresponding defect; the relevant deformations identified break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. For the partial twists of O(3), we derive the flow of the symmetry-preserving untwisted zero-mode mass generated by the bulk interaction. Its weak-coupling runaway near four dimensions motivates a careful distinction between the microscopic absence of pinning, the free reference background, and a possible infrared defect fixed point in three dimensions. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist, turning the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization for exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.

items.title: SHAPE: a sparse Hamiltonian approach for prescribing eigenstates in metamaterials
authors: Yutao Chen, Tao Xiao, Jing Li, Aodong Li, Biye Xie
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenstates, have enabled the development of devices with diverse functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenstates are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). Here we develop SHAPE, a sparse Hamiltonian approach that enables the realization of prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates in physically realizable metamaterials. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites ($|E_{\mathrm{LR}}| = |\partial\Omega|$), independent of the state interior or lattice size. The Hamiltonians are further spectrally reshaped to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. We provide a database of over 100 target states and a customizable design program, demonstrating the generality and extensibility of our method. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.

items.title: Maximum-Entropy Ensemble of Quantum Subsystems with a Fixed Average State
authors: Charlie Shakeshaft, Christopher David White, Harry J. D. Miller
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The reduced density matrices of Haar-random bipartite states form a fixed-trace version of the Wishart ensemble of random matrices, with an asymptotic eigenvalue density given by the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) law. We establish a similar universal form for the maximum-entropy distribution of mixed states subject to a fixed ensemble average, arguing that its eigenvalue density converges asymptotically to that of the correlated Wishart ensemble (CWE). The density is thus obtained by a free multiplicative convolution formula, which we apply to the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) with a thermal average state to derive a high-temperature leading-order correction to the MP law. We then consider measurement by a random POVM on the purification of the mixed reference state. We show that the resulting mixed-state ensemble is asymptotically equivalent to the CWE, and provide confirming numerical evidence. We return to the TFIM example to compute the entanglement of the system with the ancilla after measurement, and give finite-temperature Page curves for the average entanglement entropies.

items.title: The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and proofs of this have recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $\beta$ there is $\delta(\beta)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^i\sigma_x^i\sigma_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $\beta$, whenever all $|J^i-1|\le\delta(\beta)$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. Consequently, for the easy-plane model with couplings $\sigma^x\sigma^x+\sigma^y\sigma^y+\lambda\sigma^z\sigma^z$, the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $\lambda\uparrow1$. These results rest on the annulus crossing bound of Ding, Huang and Yang, used on one finite annulus where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation, and on a sign-cluster argument with Ginibre's inequality for anisotropic planar energies. Explicit constants of another isotropic proof give decay for $\beta\le c |\log(1-\lambda)|^{1/2}$. For $n\ge4$ and $|J^i-1|\le\delta$ with $\delta$ small, at $\beta\le(1-\varepsilon)|\log\delta|/(2\pi)$ spin one-point functions decay exponentially away from the boundary under every boundary condition, and two-point functions decay, both on the scale $e^{\pi\beta+O(\sqrt{\beta\log\beta})}$. This is the $O(4)$ threshold: for $n=4$ it matches the renormalization-group crossover to leading order; for $n\ge5$ it lies below the prediction. This part is conditional on estimates of a recent manuscript on the $O(4)$ model, which the proof transfers to anisotropic couplings at one scale; only odd observables transfer.

items.title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
authors: YuJie Liu, Dezhen Xue, Jun Sun, Xiangdong Ding, Zhibin Gao, Turab Lookman
items.summary: -cross Abstract: General-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rival domain-specific pipelines on scientific prediction, but their performance under distribution shift is untested. Across six alloy and crystal-structure datasets, we benchmark LLMs against traditional, BERT-based, TabPFN, and text-regression baselines under random cross-validation and six out-of-distribution (OOD) protocols shifting input and target distributions, with severity quantified via a standardized Wasserstein distance. We isolate the LLM's advantage over k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) retrieval: it beats k-NN on all eight tasks at a fixed 5% reference budget, on seven of eight when independently optimized, and in 72.5% of 120 OOD task--protocol configurations against an optimized baseline. No model family is uniformly best; the LLM is often strongest under severe shift, and error increases with target-space but not representation-space severity. Self-reported LLM confidence tracks both shift and error, more consistently than a density-only control from the same retrieved samples, and a matched-cohort check finds no substantial evidence of memorization.

items.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

items.title: Accessing Continuous Monodromy Defects of the 3D Conformal Field Theory on the Fuzzy Sphere
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Monodromy defects are line defects at the boundary of a topological symmetry surface, around which charged operators acquire a symmetry phase. They probe how a critical system responds to an inserted symmetry flux, but their universal information at strongly coupled fixed points, in particular for a continuous family of twists, remains hard to access. Here we investigate the continuous family of $U(1)$ monodromy defect with fractional twist angles embedded in the three-dimensional $O(2)$ Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe charged defect operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy, and a displacement operator close to its protected dimension, supporting the conformal nature of the defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving scalar, and identify the charge-one defect operators as the only relevant, symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the particle--vortex duality, the U(1) monodromy defect maps to a Wilson line of fractional charge in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model, and our results then provide evidence that these Wilson lines with fractional charge are locally stable conformal lines.

items.title: Quantitative Assessment of Crystal Structure Prediction
authors: Sergio Rinc\'on, Gabriel Gonz\'alez, Nicol\'as Andrade, Rafael Vel\'asquez, Sebasti\'an Ojeda, Juanita Puentes, Nicol\'as Aparicio, Paula C\'ardenas, Pablo Arbel\'aez
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP) aims to predict a material's 3D structure from its chemical composition, with applications from energy storage to biomedical devices. Despite its importance, existing evaluation frameworks suffer from key limitations: they rely on threshold-sensitive or incomparable metrics, focus predominantly on geometric performance while overlooking physical plausibility, and fail to account for polymorphism, where a chemical composition can crystallize into multiple stable structures. In parallel, recent Symmetry-Informed CSP (SICSP) methods often report results alongside standard CSP baselines while receiving crystallographic templates at inference, which constrain the search space and make SICSP a fundamentally different task. To address these limitations, we introduce an Orientation-invariant, Polymorph-Aware, Large Benchmark (OPAL-Bench) that evaluates CSP and SICSP as separate tasks. We evaluate 7 CSP and 2 SICSP methods under OPAL-Bench across 4 datasets using threshold-free geometric and physical distance metrics. Our results show that no method dominates across all metrics, and that geometric performance is not strongly correlated with physical plausibility. We also release OPAL-CSP, an SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching baseline for the CSP track that performs competitively on geometric metrics and ranks among the best on physical ones. By unifying geometric and physical metrics under a polymorph-aware protocol, OPAL-Bench enables a more comprehensive assessment of generative quality in CSP.

items.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 thin films
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79012-8 Scaling up atomically thin light emitters remains challenging. Here, authors develop solution-processable bulk-monolayer MoS2 films that preserve monolayer optical properties and exhibit room-temperature lasing-like emission under continuous optical pumping at just a few nW.

items.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78687-3 Kondo insulator phases are traditionally found in materials with f-electrons. Here, the authors present evidence towards the realization of a tunable Kondo insulator in a monolayer WS2/bilayer WSe2 moiré superlattice.

items.title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78362-7 Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.
