items.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03499-7 Quantum channels can be used to describe the evolution of quantum states, including both unitary evolution and measurement. Now the optimal number of uses needed to learn an unknown channel to any fixed accuracy has been found.

items.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78767-4 Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

items.title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79175-4 Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. Here the authors identify a pathway controlling AGO1 nuclear import and show that AGO1 subcellular localization shapes small RNA loading and silencing outputs in plants.

items.title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
items.summary: Nature Materials, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02783-4 Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

items.title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
items.summary: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

items.title: Six-dimensional programmable ultrasonic vibration for multimodal object manipulation
items.summary: Abstract Object manipulation via external stimuli is a pivotal technology across physics, engineering, and materials science. However, the strict material requirements and complex manipulation systems of existing approaches limit the operational flexibility, functional versatility, and material adaptability. Here we present an approach for generating six-dimensional (6D) programmable ultrasonic vibration. The 6D vibration consists of three-dimensional (3D) translational vibration and 3D rotational vibration, generated through coupling and superposing of multiple longitudinal and bending vibration modes. Selective spatiotemporal combination of these vibration components enables the construction of programmable vibration fields. Most importantly, we realize multimodal manipulation of individual and collective objects positioned on a 6D vibrating surface, including trapping, translation, rotation, bounce, and reconfiguration. We demonstrate highly adaptive manipulation of objects with various shapes, materials, and scales. Furthermore, diverse applications are conducted at both the macroscale and microscale. This work opens avenues for the development of ultrasound manipulation.

items.title: Three-dimensional topological disclination in acoustic crystals
authors: Zhenxiao Zhu, Yan Meng, Minmiao Wang, Xiang Xi, Yuxin Zhong, Linyun Yang, Bei Yan, Jingming Chen, Ziyao Wang, Thomas Christensen, Caigui Jiang, Changqing Xu, Ce Shang, Zhen Gao
items.summary: Topological disclinations are rotational-symmetry-breaking lattice defects that can probe crystalline topology and offer a versatile platform for topological cavities, waveguides, and lasers. Here, Zhu et al. report a three-dimensional topological disclination that carries a fractional charge of 1/2 and hosts zero-dimensional topological bound states embedded in the bulk. The result extends disclination physics beyond layered or surface-based designs and opens new possibilities for controlling waves through the interplay of band topology and defect geometry in three dimensions.

items.title: Spin group symmetry criteria for unconventional magnetism
authors: Xun-Jiang Luo, Jin-Xin Hu, Mengli Hu, Kam Tuen Law
items.summary: Unconventional magnets combine the compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets with ferromagnet-like spin splitting, promising next-generation spintronics, yet a unified symmetry principle for their classification has been lacking. Luo et al. show that just six symmetry operations in the spin space group fully determine the dimensionality and parity of the spin splitting, yielding a complete classification that overturns established paradigms and uncovering numerous candidate materials for even- and odd-parity magnets.

items.title: Conformational dynamics of exopolysaccharides underlie biofilm matrix mechanics in Vibrio cholerae
authors: Kee-Myoung Nam, Nathan Fowler, Rajan Kandel, Yongqi Zhu, Yuchu Liu, Yi-Jhen Lai, Muhammad Faheem Hassan, Emma Gerace, Alexander J. Hinbest, Merrill Asp, Rich Olson, Ying Li, Mu-Ping Nieh, Mingjiang Zhong, Robert J. Woods, Alexis Moreau, Jing Yan
items.summary: Bacterial biofilms are encased within polymeric matrices that allow them to withstand large mechanical perturbations, but how this capability arises from individual matrix components is not well-understood. Combining experiments and simulations, Nam et al. characterize the physical properties of a key polysaccharide in the Vibrio cholerae biofilm matrix and show that it is a semiflexible polymer with unusual nanoscale conformational features that may contribute to its viscosity and, in turn, to biofilm mechanics.

items.title: Combining mass redistribution and momentum redirection for droplet-substrate interaction minimization
authors: Baixue Li, Alexander Oron, Youhua Jiang
items.summary: To minimize droplet-substrate interaction, Li et al. report a reduction in both contact area and time. Pore arrays lead to mass redistribution and momentum redirection of an impacting droplet, where the former facilitates droplet breakup into daughter droplets and the latter promotes droplet liftoff by redirecting the spreading liquids upward.

items.title: Coupled Electronic Structure and Phonon Transport Driven by Bonding Reconstruction in Ba-B-C Clathrates
items.summary: Composition-driven changes in electron count, structural symmetry and bonding environment can couple the electronic and thermal responses in a material. Here, with density-functional theory and machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), we compare cubic BaB3C3 with its B-C substituted tetragonal counterpart, BaB2C4. The additional valence electron and accompanying change in crystal symmetry drive a transition from metallic BaB3C3 to semiconducting BaB2C4 and the formation of short/strong C-C bonds. The reconstructed bonding network hardens the phonon spectrum, with the maximum frequency increasing from 800 to 900. At room temperature, the in-plane lattice thermal conductivity increases from 7.6 to 18.7 W/mK, while the thermal transport alters from isotropic to anisotropic for BaB2C4. This enhancement is associated with the strengthened bonding network, higher phonon frequencies/group velocities, longer lifetimes and larger mean free paths. Machine learning potentials accurately reproduced the DFT-level energies and forces with negligible errors, and the harmonic and anharmonic features are benchmarked against explicit first-principles calculations. Our findings demonstrate that minimal B-C substitution provides a viable strategy to link composition- and structure-associated bonding reconstruction with correlated electronic and phononic alterations.

items.title: Collective photon echoes in the Tavis-Cummings model: distribution independence, two detuning regimes, and the Dicke ladder
items.summary: An ensemble of $N$ two-level molecules prepared in its ground state and sharing a lossless cavity with a weak field does not simply absorb: the intensity collapses and then recurs, in a train of collective photon echoes. Working from the exact solution of the Tavis-Cummings model in the few-photon regime $\bar n<N$, we confirm the echo time $τ_E=4π\sqrt{N+Δ}/g$ at resonance from $N=5$ to $N=400$, and separate it from the alternative $4π\sqrt{N-\bar n+Δ}/g$ by a direct test: the recurrence period is independent of $\bar n$ to $0.8\%$ across a factor of six in $\bar n$, where the alternative predicts shifts of up to $17\%$. The initial state, the ground state, requires no preparation. The echo time is independent of the initial photon distribution - coherent, thermal, squeezed and oscillatory-squeezed distributions with variances from 2 to 34 all recur together - but the echo amplitude is not: it varies at the tens-of-percent level at fixed mean, including a factor of 1.8 with the squeezing phase. Detuning organizes the dynamics into two clean regimes separated by a fragmented crossover; the echo time in the dispersive branch is exactly one-half that of the resonant branch, a factor derived from second-order dispersive perturbation theory with leading correction $5Ng^2/δ^2$, and sufficient detuning removes the dependence on the initial Dicke state. For arbitrary initial $|r=N/2,m\rangle$, emission replaces absorption at $m\simeq-N/2+\bar n$, and the echo envelope acquires one component per step up the ladder. Lindblad simulations with all loss channels acting simultaneously, and full-Hilbert-space disorder simulations, show the first echoes to be observable at $N\sim5$-$20$ on an existing five-qubit superconducting device: the echo survives cavity decay with contrast $\sim e^{-κτ_E/2}$, photons being shielded while resident in the emitters.

items.title: Tunable Long-Range Magnetic Exchange in Adatom-Decorated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: An ab initio Embedding Model Study
items.summary: Engineering magnetic interactions in two-dimensional materials offers a promising route toward programmable magnetic phases and reconfigurable spintronic functionalities. Here, we investigate magnetic adatoms on metallic monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) as a platform for tunable indirect exchange, focusing on Fe adatoms on monolayer TaS$_2$. In the intermediate-distance regime, DFT+U calculations reveal atomic-scale oscillations in the exchange coupling between two Fe adatoms and show that biaxial strain tunes the coupling. We develop a first-principles embedding model that reproduces the DFT-calculated pair exchange and establishes a substantial RKKY contribution to the exchange; controlled comparisons further identify RKKY-mediated coupling as the primary origin of the exchange's strain tunability. These results point to combining adatom arrangement with strain as a means of engineering reconfigurable magnetic interactions in metallic monolayer TMDs.

items.title: Equation of state for hard sphere fluids across stable and metastable regimes
items.summary: We review selected equations of state (EOSs) for three-dimensional hard-sphere fluids and revise a closed-virial construction to describe stable and metastable disordered states.

items.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
items.summary: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $ε=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=α^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.

items.title: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
items.summary: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are increasingly being integrated into cryogenic quantum-sensing platforms that operate in large magnetic fields. Here, the high-field limits of these measurements were probed by characterizing the dark count response of a NbTiN SNSPD at up to 14~T using in situ control of the detector orientation and benchmarking that performance against normal detector operation in smaller magnetic fields. The detector performance is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular magnetic fields rapidly reduce the usable bias-current range, whereas near-parallel alignment enables operation at substantially larger total fields, with a finite operating margin retained to 12~T and measurable dark-count response at the 14~T field limit. The angular dependence is governed predominantly by the perpendicular component of the magnetic field, consistent with vortex-mediated suppression of the superconducting current scale. The same field-dependent current scale also determines the electrical pulse amplitude, linking high-field detector operation directly to readout performance. These results establish a practical route for deploying SNSPDs in multi-tesla quantum-sensing and high-field cryogenic experiments.

items.title: Predicting Coherent B2 Stability in Ru-Containing Refractory Alloys Through Thermodynamic Elastic Design Maps
items.summary: The development of next-generation refractory superalloys is fundamentally constrained by competing requirements of high thermodynamic stability and low interfacial energy. Ru-based B2 intermetallics possess strong intrinsic ordering, but their use as coherent reinforcing phases requires balancing formation enthalpy against elastic strain. Here, we present a physics-guided machine-learning framework that integrates high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), Random Forest screening, and symbolic regression to map this design space. The approach addresses the "binary paradox" observed in recent experimental studies, where strongly ordered Ru-refractory compounds do not necessarily achieve the highest solvus temperatures. The resulting closed-form relation, T_solvus ~ 0.11(Delta H/Delta S) - 20000|delta|, quantifies the competing effects of thermodynamic stabilization and lattice misfit. Because the electronic-structure calculations are static 0 K calculations, the relation is treated as an effective calibrated design equation rather than a directly calculated finite-temperature free-energy boundary. The model is benchmarked against published B2 solvus measurements, while calculated formation enthalpies and lattice parameters are independently compared with calorimetric and diffraction data. Within the fitted relation, a 1% lattice misfit corresponds to an effective solvus penalty of approximately 200 degrees C. Al/Si substitution further shows that improved lattice matching is accompanied by reduced thermodynamic stabilization, with zero misfit near 11 at.% Al and 7 at.% Si for Nb75V25.

items.title: Entropy production decomposition and fluctuation theorems under continuous feedback: From prescribed to stochastic protocols
items.summary: When a system is driven by a prescribed protocol, the entropy production can be decomposed into the housekeeping and non-autonomous contributions, each satisfying a fluctuation theorem. Under feedback control, however, the feedback parameter depends on measurement outcomes rather than following a prescribed protocol. To study how the decomposition changes, we consider an overdamped Brownian particle at position $x$ with a low-pass-filtered measurement signal $D$ as the feedback parameter. Regarding each realization of $D$ as a stochastic protocol, we derive fluctuation theorems for the entropy production associated with the dynamics of $x$ and of $D$, and interpret them in terms of the information flow. For a solvable harmonic model, we map the dynamics onto an autonomous system in which the measurement and filtering process acts as an effective thermal bath. Feedback cooling thus corresponds to heat conduction from the physical bath through the particle to this colder bath, and the information flow can be interpreted as the entropy associated with the heat conduction between $x$ and $D$. We verify these results by numerical simulations.

items.title: Quantifying sample heating by ablation-plasma x-rays in laser-driven shock experiments
items.summary: Sample preheat due to absorption of x-rays emitted by an ablation plasma has long been a source of uncertainty in laser-driven dynamic compression experiments. This unknown heating complicates interpretation of experiments designed to reach well-defined thermodynamic states, such as the principal Hugoniot, particularly because the pressure drive and sample heating occur simultaneously and are difficult to disentangle. Here, we quantify sample heating from x-rays using a unique experimental design in which the sample is heated prior to the arrival of the pressure wave. Using in situ x-ray diffraction, we relate lattice expansion to temperature within a 1-um-thick Au sample for commonly used 25-um and 75-um-thick Kapton-B (polyimide) ablators over a range of laser irradiances. Heating, sufficient to melt Au (Delta T ~ 1050 K), is observed for 25-um-thick polyimide ablators, which is significantly enhanced by the addition of a 0.2-um Al flash coating. In contrast, heating is strongly suppressed for 75-um-thick, non-Al-coated Kapton-B, with no measurable heating observed in 2.5-um-thick Ti or 1-um-thick Fe samples at laser irradiances up to 1.2 x 10^13 W/cm^2. .

items.title: The maximum packing fraction of disordered bidisperse discs: theory and predictions
items.summary: Predicting the highest packing fraction that disordered packing of bidisperse discs can achieve, $φ_{max}$, is an important unresolved problem. Such a predictive theory is hindered by the density dependence on the packing protocol and by ensuring disorder. In bidisperse packings, this is more complicated because $φ_{max}$ is not a number but a function of the disc species size ratio, $D$, and one of the disc species concentration, $p$. These difficulties have been overcome in monodisperse disc packings by using the cell order distribution (COD)~\cite{Bl21}. Focusing on size ratios that prohibit rattlers, a COD-based theory is constructed here. It introduces bidisperse statistical closure equations, which combine an explicit disorder criterion with consistent cell and edge statistics, and yields $φ_{max}(p,D)$ and structural predictions. The a-priori disorder-guaranteeing criterion proposed here ensures fast exponential a decay of the occurrence probability of ordered clusters with size. Using a constrained maximum-entropy analysis to ensure maximum disorder, the occurrence probabilities of all the possible cell and edge configurations are derived in terms of $p$ and $D$ and they are found to be binomial. All the results are assembled to yield an exact prediction of $φ_{max}(p,D)$.

items.title: Hidden symmetry at the diabolical points of a biaxial spin
items.summary: In a rotated frame the biaxial spin Hamiltonian $k_1S_x^2+k_2S_y^2-\mathbf{h}\cdot\mathbf{S}$ is a finite tight-binding chain whose hopping amplitudes are tuned by the applied field. A chain with no vanishing hopping has a nondegenerate spectrum, so a degeneracy can occur only where the field severs the chain. At every point of the diabolical-point lattice proven exact by Keçecioğlu and Garg, the chain is severed in two different rotated frames, at two bonds that are labeled independently. We write the two severings as two spectral-cut projectors. These are explicit polynomials in two field-independent spin components; they commute with the Hamiltonian at that point but not with each other. This gives a concrete form to the hidden symmetry anticipated by Garg: on the degenerate subspace the two projectors generate a pseudospin SU(2) that commutes with the Hamiltonian. The rank of a pairing operator built from them gives the multiplicity of every lattice point, without the continuity and topological argument used previously. Because the two partners of a doublet occupy disjoint stretches of the chain, the splitting determinant factorizes exactly and has a fixed negative sign. Every degeneracy of the model is therefore a linear cone, all cones have the same orientation, and the lower level carries Chern charge $-1$ for the Berry connection $i\langleψ|\nablaψ\rangle$.

items.title: Folding of multishape metamaterials guided by plasticity
items.summary: Multishape metamaterials can morph into several different shapes and offer exciting prospects in areas as diverse as tunable optics, wearable electronics, soft robotics, and aerospace. Yet, multishape metamaterials are typically actuated with complex multiaxial or multiphysics loading. Here, we introduce a uniaxial folding strategy that turns kirigami, 2D sheets patterned with cuts, into multishape metamaterials with tunable rigidity. Our folding approach leverages plasticity and loading history to guide multiple and tunable distinct shape changes upon cycles of stretching and compression. The deployed shapes exhibit a wide range of mechanical properties spanning three orders of magnitude. Self-guided plastic folding provides a uniquely scalable route to deploy load-bearing metamaterials from the micrometer up to the industrial scale.

items.title: Fractionalized Fermi liquids with the ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz
items.summary: Fractionalized Fermi liquids ($\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$), elusive metallic states characterized by fractionalized quasiparticles alongside conventional ones and defying Luttinger's theorem, are prime candidates for the pseudogap regime of underdoped cuprates. We show that a $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$ phase emerges in the single-band $t$-$J$ model through a simple ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz, optimized at the cost of a mean-field calculation. The resulting temperature-doping phase diagram encompasses a low-doping $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$, a $d$-wave superconducting dome, and an overdoped conventional Fermi liquid, thereby reproducing key qualitative features of cuprate phenomenology.

items.title: Phase Transitions of Polar Nematic Liquid Crystals Driven by Electrostatics and Flexoelectricity
items.summary: Polar liquid crystals can exhibit a series of phases and phase transitions, from the conventional nematic phase at high temperature to a modulated nematic (antiferroelectric) phase at intermediate temperature, and then to a uniform polar (ferroelectric) phase at lower temperature. Here, we develop a theory for this phase behavior. The theory is based on a competition between flexoelectricity (which favors splay in the modulated phase) and electrostatics (which provides an energy penalty for splay). Minimizing the free energy leads to differential equations that describe the spatial variation of the director, the polar order, and the electric potential. By solving the differential equations numerically, we determine the structure of the antiferroelectric phase. At high temperature, the modulated structure is sinusoidal. At lower temperature, it crosses over to a structure of wide domains separated by narrow domain walls. These numerical solutions can be compared with simplified models that apply near the phase transitions.

items.title: Electric birefringence in Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics
items.summary: The fermion sector of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics is integrated functionally to generate a non-linear electrodynamics, that it is called Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics. A non-local Chern-Simons topological term is added to the original lagrangian of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics in which a most complete electrodynamics gauge invariant in 1+2 dimensions is proposed. As consequence of the fermionic sector, we obtain a non-linear contribution in the electromagnetic fields that breaks the Lorentz symmetry due to Fermi velocity. From the Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics, we study the properties of the plane wave propagating in a planar medium under an uniform and constant electromagnetic background field. The properties of the planar material are discussed through the electric permittivity tensor and magnetic permeability, that are functions of the frequency, wavelength and of the background fields. The dispersion relations and the refractive index are calculated in the presence of a uniform magnetic field, and also in the case only of an electric background field. The birefringence phenomenon emerges only when the electric background field is considered.

items.title: Mott transitions in Dirac nodal-line semimetals
items.summary: Nodal-line semimetals provide a natural setting to investigate how the geometry of a nodal manifold affects interaction-driven quantum phase transitions. Here, we study the Hubbard model on a cubic lattice supporting either nodal-point (cubic $π$-flux model) or nodal-line semimetallic states using mean-field theory, determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, and a weak-coupling renormalization-group (RG) analysis. In both cases, antiferromagnetic order develops only above a finite interaction strength, with the nodal-line system exhibiting a smaller critical coupling due to its enhanced low-energy density of states and markedly stronger finite-size effects. For the nodal-point model, the quantum critical behavior is compatible with $(3+1)$-dimensional Gross--Neveu mean-field scaling. In contrast, the weak-coupling RG reveals that the nodal line itself is unstable against interactions: although the Hubbard interaction is perturbatively irrelevant, its second-order self-energy generates a symmetry-allowed relevant term proportional to $U^2\cos k_z$, reconstructing the nodal line into isolated, strongly anisotropic nodal points. This weak-coupling reconstruction is distinct from the strong-coupling antiferromagnetic transition and highlights the role of nodal-manifold geometry in interacting semimetals.

items.title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
items.summary: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.

items.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
items.summary: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

items.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
items.summary: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

items.title: What Can Next Generation Ultrafast Light Sources Tell Us About Quantum Materials?
items.summary: Ultrafast spectroscopy of quantum materials has emerged as a principle application of modern ultrafast optical sources. Measurements made with ultrashort pulses allow the normally strongly coupled internal degrees of freedom inside these systems to be de-coupled in the time-domain, revealing the key interactions for the different orders that lead to dramatic emergent phenomena. This has naturally motivated a wide range of experiments, and quantum materials have now been studied with ultrafast sources spanning from the hard X-ray to the THz, with fields intense enough to create non-equilibrium states, and using pulses down to the attosecond duration. As the optical spectroscopist's toolbox becomes increasingly complete, it is worth pausing and reflecting on what are the capabilities that we currently lack for examining quantum materials, and what are the problems that require the next generation of ultrafast sources now coming on-line or being designed. Here I will offer an overview of the remaining missing capabilities in ultrafast optical sources as required for studying quantum materials, and identify some outstanding problems where I believe these new sources can provide decisive impact in our understanding of quantum and strongly-correlated materials.

items.title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
items.summary: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically non-perturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality, characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd$_2$(Si$_{1-x}$Ge$_x$)$_2$, where, depending on $x$ and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for $x \approx 0.1$ by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

items.title: A New High $γ$-$γ'$ Fraction Polycrystalline Co/Ni Superalloy
items.summary: An ingot-processable Co/Ni-based $γ/γ'$ superalloy has been developed for wrought parts in aircraft engines. An 8.5 kg VIM ingot was homogenised and hot rolled to a true strain of 1. A heat treatment was then developed to produce 50% $γ'$ and a grain size of 142 $μ$m. High-temperature tensile testing showed yield strengths of 820 MPa at 700 $^\circ$C, 785 MPa at 800 $^\circ$C and 783 MPa at 850 $^\circ$C. Creep tests at 750 $^\circ$C/600 MPa and 800 $^\circ$C/300 MPa demonstrated reduced minimum creep rates and extended rupture lives relative to current wrought Ni-base alloys. Oxidation at 800 $^\circ$C for 100 h formed a 1 $μ$m dual chromia/alumina scale with minimal subsurface degradation. Long-term exposure at 800 $^\circ$C for 8000 h showed limited $γ'$ coarsening and no deleterious intermetallic or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.

items.title: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light
items.summary: Theoretical descriptions of the quantum electrodynamical interaction between fast electrons and nanostructures conventionally rely on standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED), which, when applied to bounded objects in vacuum, formally requires an asymptotic limiting procedure to account for free-space radiation modes. To explicitly incorporate these modes from the outset, we employ the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), which independently quantizes both the asymptotic scattering modes and the electromagnetic field generated by dissipative material sources. Utilizing an exact second-order Magnus expansion, we derive a closed-form, nonperturbative master formula for the transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange probability. In the unilluminated regime, we demonstrate that at finite nanostructure temperatures, the vacuum scattering and thermal material fluctuations do not mathematically recombine into the total imaginary part of the dyadic Green's function. This breakdown does not violate the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, because the explicit zero-temperature scattering field acts as an independent dynamical system that maintains the configuration out of global thermodynamic equilibrium. This fundamental separation reveals an intrinsic Stokes--Anti-Stokes asymmetry, yielding distinct transverse diffraction patterns for energy loss and thermal energy gain, and establishing a generalized detailed-balance relation that governs the radiative reduction of the apparent temperature in nanoscale electron thermometry. In the illuminated regime, our framework rigorously incorporates quantum-optical states into macroscopic dissipative electrodynamics, demonstrating that...

items.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
items.summary: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

items.title: What Hall Measures in Strongly Correlated Metals
items.summary: The Hall effect provides a sensitive probe of electronic correlations in strongly interacting metals, yet its microscopic interpretation beyond quasiparticle transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a Liouvillian formulation of the Hall conductivity that organizes the response into different classes of flux-sensitive many-body interference operators. Using a Schrieffer-Wolff transformation of the Hubbard model, we identify how projected charge motion and virtual hopping processes contribute to oriented trajectories enclosing magnetic flux. A high-temperature expansion reveals a hierarchy of inverse-temperature contributions associated with these interference processes. This framework provides a possible microscopic interpretation of the integer power laws previously observed in determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, which emerge at temperatures below the regime where the expansion is formally controlled. Our results highlight the sensitivity of Hall transport to coherent many-body dynamics and establish a connection between lattice geometry, electronic correlations, and transverse charge response.

items.title: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
items.summary: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has continuously broadened their applicability to increasingly complex systems in chemistry and materials science. Extending MLPs to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, however, is still challenging as it requires the consideration of electrode potentials and electric fields in the atomic interactions. Such approaches have emerged only recently, and although the field is evolving rapidly, further conceptual advances are still needed for carrying out reliable simulations at finite temperature under applied potential. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview about recent progress in the atomistic simulation of electrified interfaces using MLPs. Current developments fall into three different categories. The first comprises linear response models that describe polarisation, polarisability, and Born effective charges, extending conventional MLPs to finite electric fields. The second includes methods that directly learn a field-dependent potential energy surface. The third consists of a series of hybrid approaches combining classical models with machine learning. Although still under active development, these methods represent a major step toward more realistic simulations approaching the quality of electronic structure calculations. Finally, we discuss open challenges and possible future directions for advancing MLP-based simulations aiming for a bottom-up understanding of atomistic processes at electrified interfaces.

items.title: Eigenvalue Crossings and Discontinuous BBP Transitions in Spiked Euclidean Random Matrices
items.summary: We study the recovery of a rank-one signal embedded in a symmetric Euclidean random matrix, whose dense and geometrically correlated entries generally lack rotational invariance. We show that signal recovery through the leading eigenvector is governed by a competition between the principal directions of the noise and the signal. In particular, the signal may already be encoded in a subleading eigendirection, while remaining undetected by the leading principal component. As the signal strength increases, a crossing between competing eigenvalues can change their ordering, causing the leading eigenvector to switch abruptly from a noise-dominated to a signal-bearing direction. This mechanism gives rise to a discontinuous BBP-type transition, in which the overlap with the signal jumps from zero to a finite value. Using the replica method, we reduce the problem to a Fredholm eigenvalue equation and derive general criteria for the existence of a positive recovery threshold, expressed in terms of the unperturbed spectral edge, the spike mean and the spatial averages of the principal eigenfunctions. We obtain analytically the limiting largest eigenvalue, eigenvector-component distribution and signal overlap, and illustrate the results with explicit solutions for quadratic distance and rank-two kernels, finding excellent agreement with numerical diagonalisation.

items.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
items.summary: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

items.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
items.summary: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

items.title: Band geometry, Anderson's theorem, and vortex nucleation in unconventional 2D superconductors
items.summary: Motivated by the recent discovery of chiral superconductors in 2d materials, we study the effects of disorder on superconductivity in materials with non-trivial band geometry. First, we show how Anderson's theorem and the conventional Abrikosov-Gorkov description of disorder-induced pair breaking are modified by the structure of the normal-state Bloch functions. We apply these results to twisted MoTe2 and show that a BCS pairing mechanism for the observed superconductor is in tension with the measured normal state residual resistivity. Second, we study whether random potential disorder can nucleate superconducting vortices in a chiral time- reversal-breaking superconductor. We show that, for a superconductor stabilized by the usual BCS mechanism, weak disorder does not induce a vortex glass phase, in contrast to superconductivity formed from an anyon fluid.

items.title: Non-Bloch Topology of Frustrated Non-Hermitian Flat Bands
items.summary: Frustrated lattices with exactly flat bands and compact localized states provide an ideal setting to uncover the topology of flat bands, leading to intriguing physics in two dimensions. Extending from Hermitian to non-Hermitian systems, however, band structures are drastically changed by the non-Hermitian skin effect, which is less well understood beyond one dimension. Here, we construct a broad class of two-dimensional frustrated non-Hermitian lattice models with exactly flat bands which can be naturally described in a non-Bloch band theory. Using non-Hermitian breathing Kagome and checkerboard models as illustrations, we reveal how flat bands acquire a basis-independent skin effect induced by the other bands; in the breathing Kagome model it appears exactly when the flat band enters the area spanned by the periodic-boundary spectra of the dispersive bands. A flat band becomes singular when its eigenvectors hold immovable discontinuities at band crossings. Such singularity in non-Hermitian systems is sensitive to boundary conditions and unprotected by band flatness. Non-Bloch topology underlying is uncovered in a bulk-boundary correspondence with the formation of a singular band touching in the bulk and a robust flat band skin mode on the boundary. We present a geometric approach to construct this boundary skin mode from a macroscopic sum of compact localized skin modes and trace its topological origin to two linearly independent noncontractible loop states on a non-Bloch torus. To characterize the correspondence, an invariant is proposed based on biorthogonal polarization of the zero-energy corner mode. Breaking exact flatness, we further realize nearly flat non-Bloch Chern bands.

items.title: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
items.summary: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde Γ$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.

items.title: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from the Dynamical Structure Factor
items.summary: Identifying the microscopic interactions governing a quantum system is essential for developing predictive theories of materials and validating quantum technologies. Despite considerable progress, learning Hamiltonians from realistic experimental data remains a challenge. Motivated by neutron scattering and quantum simulations, we study the problem of learning a quantum Hamiltonian from the dynamical structure factor (DSF), which captures two-point correlation data in quantum magnets. We show that the DSF encodes sufficient information to efficiently reconstruct broad classes of quantum Hamiltonians. Our approach exploits simple relations between low-order spectral moments of the DSF and microscopic couplings, giving rise to three complementary Hamiltonian tomography protocols based on the high-temperature expansion, strong-field polarization, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. The framework we introduce establishes practical and robust Hamiltonian learning from common experimental data, with potentially immediate application to neutron scattering experiments.

items.title: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
items.summary: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $Σ\sim\sqrtω$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $Σ\simω\log(1/ω)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $ω/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.

items.title: Potts Order Preempts Emergence of 2-Form U(1) Spin Liquidity in Three-Dimensional Spin Vorticity Models
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) spin vorticity models (SVMs) have been proposed to realize an exotic 2-form U(1) classical spin liquid (CSL), characterized by a zero-curl constraint, string excitations, and deconfined fluctuating membranes. A previous numerical study [PRB 111, 064417 (2025)] uncovered a puzzle in the pyrochlore lattice SVM: despite exhibiting pinch points characteristic of a U(1) spin liquid, it also develops weak all-in--all-out (AIAO) order. Here, we show that the emergence of the 2-form CSL in 3D SVMs is preempted by an intrinsic instability towards entropy-driven height locking. We establish this by resolving the ground state constraints using a height mapping, which we further relate to a 3-state Potts antiferromagnet. This identifies the pyrochlore's weak AIAO order as permutationally symmetric sublattice (PSS) order, albeit with an exceptionally weak locking strength. We extend the SVM to lattices of corner-sharing octahedra and cubes, where we identify the alternative broken-sublattice-symmetry (BSS) order, a hidden order without magnetic Bragg peaks coexisting with collective paramagnetism. All three models undergo a 3D Ising transition consistent with a symmetry-allowed locking potential in the coarse-grained height theory. The spin liquid persists over intermediate length and temperature scales, but a critical Coulomb ground state ensemble fails to materialize, its correlations cut off by the finite locking length. These findings illustrate how microscopic constraints can determine the ultimate stability of emergent gauge theories in frustrated spin systems.

items.title: Lithium redistribution and electrode degradation in commercial NMC/Graphite and LCO/Graphite cells under high-rate cycling conditions
items.summary: Fast charging accelerates degradation in lithium-ion batteries, but the effects of cathode chemistry and charging protocol remain difficult to separate. Here, commercial NMC811/graphite (200 mAh) and LCO/graphite (45 mAh) coin cells were cycled for 100 cycles at 0.3C, 1C, 2C, and 3C, followed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and nuclear reaction analysis (NRA). Both cell types exhibited a transition in cycling stability between 1C and 2C. NMC811/graphite retained approximately 99.7% of its initial discharge capacity at 0.3C and 1C, decreasing to 72.3% at 2C and 63.5% at 3C, while LCO/graphite retained only 11.1% at 2C. NRA revealed maximum lithium accumulation in graphite anodes at 2C for both chemistries, supported by SEM observations of granular surface deposits. XRD showed rate-dependent shifts in cathode (003) and graphite (002) reflections, indicating structural changes during cycling. The lower lithium accumulation at 3C was associated with reduced charge throughput, while the LCO/graphite 3C condition was limited by its charging protocol. These findings highlight the importance of anode-side degradation and charging protocols in interpreting high-rate cycling performance of commercial lithium-ion batteries.

items.title: Tuning of quantum nanoscaled friction within the Prandtl-Tomlinson model
items.summary: Nanoscaled is a fundamental tribological phenomenon with complex behavior of its dynamical force. Here, we utilize the Prandtl-Tomlinson framework to investigate systematically the different means of control of the frictional force at the quantum and classical levels. It is found that the frictional dynamics can be controlled by the corrugation and characteristic length ratio parameters dependent upon properties of the nanoparticle-chain system. In addition to the stick-slip regime, other types of motion are uncovered, highlighting the richness of the frictional dynamics. The importance of Landau-Zener tunneling for the quantum motion is also analyzed. These findings provide valuable insights for interpreting experimental observations and controlling quantum frictional behavior in nanoscale systems.

items.title: Heterogeneous ice nucleation with TIP4P/Ice: the role of lattice mismatch
items.summary: Ice formation, a crucial phase transition for life on Earth, mainly occurs through heterogeneous nucleation on a solid substrate. Despite the importance of this phenomenon, the correlation between the structure of the substrate and its ability to induce ice nucleation remains poorly understood. In this work, we use molecular dynamics simulations with an atomistic model of water to investigate how the lattice mismatch affects the ability of the substrate to nucleate ice. To unambiguously quantify the mismatch, we use substrates with a stretched ice structure. We put the substrate in contact with supercooled water and determine the temperature at which ice spontaneously nucleates during the course of the simulations. We find that the nucleation temperature decreases by $\sim$ 5-6 K for each percent by which the substrate lattice is stretched relative to that of ice. This trend is similar to that previously obtained with a coarse-grained water model [Camarillo et al., J. Chem. Phys. 160, 134505 (2024)]. \textcolor{black}{The substrate induces a fluctuating network of subcritical ice-like clusters, from which a spherical-cap-shaped supercritical nucleus eventually emerges stochastically.} Using Classical Nucleation Theory, combine previously reported homogeneous nucleation rates with heterogeneous nucleation rates computed in this work to estimate key heterogeneous nucleation parameters, including the nucleation barrier, the kinetic pre-factor, and the contact angle. The latter is consistent with a microscopic visualization of nucleation trajectories, supporting the applicability of Classical Nucleation Theory to describe a microscopic phenomenon such as heterogeneous ice nucleation.

items.title: Probing chiral topological order of the Kitaev honeycomb on a trapped ion processor
items.summary: Kitaev's honeycomb model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable system hosting a quantum spin liquid with non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected edge modes, offering a platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, real candidate Kitaev materials invariably include complex secondary interactions that obscure the realization of spin-liquid behavior and demand novel quantum computational approaches for efficient simulation. Here we report quantum simulations of a 22-site Kitaev honeycomb lattice on a trapped-ion quantum processor, without and with non-integrable Heisenberg interactions that are present in real materials. We develop efficient quantum circuits for ground-state preparation, achieving high accuracy with energy errors equivalent to an effective temperature $\approx 0.2$ (in units of the Kitaev interactions), consistent with the experimentally relevant spin-liquid regime. Starting from these states, we apply controlled perturbations and measure time-dependent spin correlations along the system's edge. In the non-Abelian phase, we observe chiral edge dynamics consistent with a non-zero Chern number, a hallmark of chiral topological order, which vanishes upon transition to the Abelian toric code phase. Extending to the non-integrable Kitaev-Heisenberg model, we find that weak Heisenberg interactions preserve chiral edge dynamics, while stronger couplings suppress them, signaling the breakdown of topological protection. These simulations establish edge-mode dynamical simulations on quantum computers as a staple technique to understand the topological and chiral phases of matter in Hamiltonians beyond integrability.

items.title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models
items.summary: Universal density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonian models trained across broad chemical and structural spaces offer an efficient route from atomic structure to electronic properties. However, estimating prediction uncertainty alongside fast Hamiltonian predictions remains a challenge. In this work, we present EviDTB, an evidential deep regression approach for tight-binding DFT Hamiltonians that effectively estimates prediction uncertainty in a single forward pass. Compared with deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation (MVE), EviDTB achieves a better balance between computational cost and uncertainty-quantification performance. On 5,478 held-out test structures, EviDTB achieves a full spin--orbit-coupled (SOC) Hamiltonian matrix-element mean absolute error of 0.622meV. Its mean uncertainty per atom correlates with the mean local squared prediction error (Spearman $ρ=0.812$); removing the 15% most uncertain structures reduces the 99th percentile of this error by 78%, from 16.63 to 3.72eV$^2$. This score offers a practical way to prioritize candidates for first-principles verification. We hope that combining fast Hamiltonian prediction with uncertainty-guided screening will accelerate the search for materials with desirable electronic properties.

items.title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
items.summary: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

Issue Editorial Masthead
Toward Unified and Accurate Description of Multidimensional Nuclear Observables via a Prior-Informed Large Language Model
authors: Shijie Guo, 世杰 郭, Shouyu Wang, 守宇 王, Enhong Wang, 恩宏 王, Zhongming Niu, 中明 牛, Yiming Ding and 一鸣 丁
items.summary: A prior-informed large language model (LLM)-driven multi-task learning framework is proposed for the unified and accurate description of multiple nuclear observables. By fine-tuning the pre-trained DeepSeek-R1-1.5B model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), lightweight adapters are introduced while preserving general pre-trained parameters. Under a causal language modeling paradigm, the model is trained autoregressively on deviations between experimental and theoretical values. Significant accuracy improvements are achieved across seven observables, including charge radii, masses, binding energies, separation energies, and decay energies, with the training loss decreasing by over 98% across all tasks. This demonstrates that the LLM-based framework, through structured prior embedding, offers an efficient and shared approach for multi-task regression in fundamental nuclear properties.

items.title: On the Precise Boundary of the Néel Antiferromagnetic Phase in the Shastry-Sutherland Model
authors: Rongyi Lv, 融一 吕, Xiangjian Qian, 湘坚 钱, Mingpu Qin and 明普 秦
items.summary: The ground state phase diagram of the Shastry-Sutherland model remains controversial. In particular, the nature of the transition between the plaquette valence bond solid (PVBS) phase and the Néel antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase is still under debate. While some studies suggest a direct transition between the two phases, others propose the existence of a narrow intermediate quantum spin liquid regime. To address this issue, we perform large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group calculations to determine the Néel AFM phase boundary in the Shastry-Sutherland model. By applying staggered boundary pinning fields and directly measuring the bulk staggered magnetization, and through systematic extrapolations with respect to truncation error as well as careful finite-size scaling, we find that the staggered magnetization remains finite across the controversial region 0.78 ≲J1/J2 ≤ 0.81, which was suggested to host a quantum spin liquid phase in some studies. Together with the previously established consensus placing the PVBS phase boundary at J1/J2 ≈ 0.78, these results, within the resolution of the present calculations, provide evidence against the existence of an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase and support a direct PVBS–Néel AFM transition in the Shastry-Sutherland model.

items.title: Discovery of NIR-II nanocrystals Ag3AuSe2 with near-unity quantum yield
items.summary: ABSTRACT The development of second near-infrared (NIR-II) emitting nanocrystals (NCs) with unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) is paramount for deep-tissue bioimaging and high-efficiency optoelectronics; however, the PLQY decreases markedly as the emission shifts to longer wavelengths. Herein, we have discovered a novel Ag 3 AuSe 2 (fischesserite) NC system that extends this PLQY-wavelength frontier into the long-wavelength regime, achieving a near-unity absolute PLQY of 98.9% at 1000 nm with a monoexponential decay time of 4.1 µs. The synthesis of the near-single-crystal Ag 3 AuSe 2 NCs hinges on the employment of an Au(I)-octanethiolate coordination polymer, [Au(OTT)] n , as the Au precursor. This precursor enables the regulated release of active gold species and provides a mild redox environment, which are essential for improving crystal quality and suppressing interfacial defects otherwise induced by side reactions. The exceptional brightness of these NCs provides a new paradigm for ultra-high signal-to-noise ratio imaging, fundamentally reshaping the application landscape for NIR-II emitters.

items.title: 2D quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by highly-bichromatic fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort and Amelle Zaïr
items.summary: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.

items.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (QKD) relies on coherent detection. Conventional coherent receivers typically use an optical 90° hybrid and two balanced photodetectors providing robust phase-diversity detection. Here, we introduce and characterize a simplified receiver architecture based on a symmetric 3 × 3 beam splitter (BS) and three single-ended photodetectors for continuous-variable QKD. Results demonstrate that the 3 × 3 BS-based architecture provides similar performance to conventional ones while reducing optical-hardware complexity.

items.title: Magnon-mediated cooling by heating in a spin-selective quantum dot system
items.summary: We demonstrate how nonequilibrium magnons can drive the cooling by heating effect in a spin-selective quantum dot system. The mechanism relies on magnon-assisted spin-flip transitions that transfer electrons between two ferromagnetic electrodes maintained at different temperatures, with the magnetic insulator acting as the high-temperature energy source. In the limit of fully spin-polarized antiparallel electrodes, the transport enters a tight-coupling regime in which each absorbed magnon is accompanied by the transfer of a single electron. This one-to-one correspondence directly links the cooling power to the heat supplied by the magnonic reservoir and enables the thermodynamic performance to approach its upper bound. We further show how finite spin polarization introduces parasitic spin channels that suppress cooling and reduce the operating range. An extended dual quantum dot configuration restores cooling by heating without net charge current and enhances the cooling power. Our results establish magnons as a distinct microscopic energy carrier for cooling by heating and provide a route toward its realization in solid-state spin-caloritronic systems.

items.title: Particle dynamics in constant synthetic non-abelian fields: I. the classical treatment
authors: Subramanya Bhat K N, Amita Das, Bhooshan Paradkar and V Ravishankar
items.summary: Yang–Mills (YM) theory has evolved beyond its origins in the strong interaction to become an effective framework for condensed matter, ultracold atomic, and photonic systems, where synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields enable phenomena such as spin transport, the spin-Hall effect, and polarization control. These systems provide access to gauge-field dynamics beyond the reach of high-energy experiments. In all the above mentioned cases, the state of the system evolves in an effective external YM field. Here, we report the results of a classical study (as preparatory for a full quantum study) of particle dynamics in constant gauge fields produced by constant gauge potentials, by focusing on configurations that are experimentally relevant. We show that consequences such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlation between charge and color dynamics have a direct bearing on the physical phenomena observed, especially in experiments involving charge and spin transports. More generally, this work also shows how the low energy systems can act as laboratories to probe quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu-Yang ambiguity.

items.title: Observing quantum-classical correspondence through optical path integrals
authors: Li-Man Tian, Yunfei Wang, Ying Zhou, Chang Li, Shanchao Zhang, Xuan Dai, Bai-Chuan Long, Hui Yan, Shi-Liang Zhu and Yong-Li Wen
items.summary: The quantum–classical correspondence (QCC) describes how quantum systems recover classical behavior in the semiclassical limit. One of the crucial mechanisms to this correspondence is the concept of action, which governs dynamics in both classical mechanics and quantum path integrals. Despite its fundamental importance, experimental access to the action of individual quantum paths remains crucial yet challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a method to measure the action of quantum paths between fixed spacetime points, based on weak-value measurement techniques. By introducing and analyzing the spectrum of the norm of the action gradient, we identify not only single but also multiple stationary-action paths in systems exhibiting complex QCC. Using an optical setup that simulates photon propagation in free space and under an impulsive potential, we reconstruct pathwise actions and observe sharp dips in the spectrum that correspond precisely to classical trajectories. This work provides a framework for directly accessing and analyzing the action, opening new avenues for experimentally exploring the QCC.

items.title: Algebraic structures of the Lindblad equation
authors: Leonel Bixano, Guillermo López-Alvarez, Victor Alberto Cruz-Barriguete, Víctor Guadalupe Ibarra-Sierra, José Luis Cardoso, Juan Carlos Sandoval-Santana and Alejandro Kunold
items.summary: We investigate the algebraic structure underlying the Lindblad equation for finite-dimensional open quantum systems. Using an orthonormal Hermitian operator basis, we represent the Liouville superoperator in a model-independent basis of Hermitian superoperators realizing the standard left–right multiplication maps. We express their multiplication, commutator, and anticommutator relations explicitly in terms of the Lie and Jordan structure constants of the underlying operator basis. This formulation makes explicit how dissipative contributions can extend the generator beyond the adjoint Lie algebra associated with purely Hamiltonian evolution. The multiplication rules allow us to derive differential equations for the expansion coefficients of the dynamical map. We further derive recursion relations for the iterative construction of the algebra in multiqubit systems. For a fixed operator basis, the algebraic data can be precomputed and reused, while the Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters enter through a single set of coefficients. Computational benchmarks compare memory usage and construction time for algebraic, direct, and standard Kronecker implementations. For the cases tested, the algebraic implementation reduces peak memory requirements and construction time relative to the direct implementation. In the benchmarks, the standard Kronecker implementation requires less memory and time than both alternatives and enables calculations for larger numbers of qubits. These findings establish the computational limitations of the present algebraic implementation alongside its explicit characterization of the underlying superoperator algebra. An accompanying Mathematica notebook provides five examples covering algebraic verification for one-, two-, and three-qubit operator bases and numerical transmon dynamics. The examples confirm agreement with the direct method, illustrate an approximate gate and population leakage beyond the computational subspace, and use Choi matrices to check Hermiticity preservation, complete positivity, and trace preservation.

items.title: Experiment-Compatible Measurement–Feedback Quantum State Preparation with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Xiaotian Nie, 晓天 聂, Tao Zhang, 韬 张, Linghui Chen and 凌辉 陈
items.summary: Ground-state preparation is a critical task in quantum simulation and quantum computing, as it enables the study of correlated phases and the generation of entangled resource states. While measurement–feedback control has emerged as a promising route to state preparation, existing schemes either rely on handcrafted, task-specific policies or are designed using full quantum-state information that is unavailable in real experiments and becomes impractical for large many-body systems. Here we develop an adaptive measurement–feedback protocol based on reinforcement learning under partial observability. The controller uses only the history of experimentally accessible measurement outcomes to choose both the measurement operator and the feedback action in real time. To make training compatible with experiments, we introduce a stochastic terminal reward built from one-shot measurements of randomly sampled Hamiltonian components, avoiding unphysical full-state reconstruction while remaining an unbiased estimator of the target energy. We demonstrate the method by preparing ground states of the Bose–Hubbard model and by generating GHZ states, establishing a scalable and hardware-compatible route to quantum state preparation.

items.title: Electron–Phonon Coupling with Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Transfer
items.summary: Spin and orbital angular momentum transfer between lattice vibrations and electrons has become an important focus beyond traditional electron–phonon coupling. Recent studies of spin–rotation coupling have shown that the rotational motion of lattice elastic vibrations can directly interact with the electron spin. Here we develop a microscopic description of the electron–phonon angular momentum coupling beyond spin–rotation coupling, which includes both the electron spin and orbital angular momentum from the relative motion of atoms in a local co-rotating lattice. We relate the lattice angular velocity to the atom-relative angular momentum through the inertia tensor, so that the lattice angular momentum, coupled to total electron angular momentum, contains both phonon spin and orbital angular momentum. The microscopic construction connects with continuum rotation descriptions, extends to non-rigid motion, and reveals discrete-lattice effects beyond the long-wavelength limit. These results provide a microscopic framework of electron–phonon coupling with spin and orbital angular momentum transfer, enabling both studies of phonon-driven electron spin and orbital dynamics and electron-driven phonon spin and orbital dynamics.

items.title: Circular Phonon Dichroism in d-Wave Altermagnets
authors: Ding Li, 顶 李, Tao Qin, 涛 秦, Jianhui Zhou and 建辉 周
items.summary: Altermagnets, a new class of collinear antiferromagnets, exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting and offer compelling advantages for antiferromagnetic spintronics. However, the magnetic order is intrinsically difficult to read out, which hinders practical applications. We propose finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism (CPD) as a direct probe that distinguishes the two opposite out-of-plane Néel vector configurations in two-dimensional d-wave altermagnets. Combining Onsager reciprocity with C2z lattice symmetry, we find that the dichroic signal reverses sign when the Néel vector is flipped for the in-plane phonon wave vectors. Moreover, a channel-resolved decomposition identifies the CPD originates from the interband coherent transitions. Representative finite-momentum cuts show pronounced dichroic asymmetric ratio, with |ηCPD| = 36%. Our work reveals that the circular-ultrasound absorption can distinguish the two opposite out-of-plane Néel vector configurations of d-wave altermagnets.
