items.title: Quantum algorithm for evaluating Lyapunov stability of non-Hermitian systems
items.summary: Stability is a fundamental property of dynamical systems, and Lyapunov theory provides a rigorous link between stability and eigenvalue distribution. By computing eigenvalues, quantum algorithms may offer potential advantages for evaluating the stability of high-dimensional systems under appropriate assumptions regarding data access and quantum resource requirements. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to efficiently resolve the complex eigenspectrum of non-Hermitian matrices and determine asymptotic stability. By employing block encoding and QSVT techniques, we implement a polynomial transformation to approximate the singular value threshold problem, enabling the localization of eigenvalues with positive real parts under appropriate requirements regarding block encoding efficiency, matrix conditioning, state overlap, and precision. We validate the method numerically on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain with local gain and loss, demonstrating accurate detection of unstable and stable cases, which is consistent with the results obtained by exact diagonalization. These results show that our quantum algorithm is a reliable and powerful tool for stability analysis and spectral characterization of high-dimensional dynamical systems.

items.title: Universal Scaling and Implications of the Apparent Anomalous Hall Voltage of Magnetic Layer with an Adjacent Conducting Layer
authors: Zhihao Yan, Qianbiao Liu, Zhengxiao Li and Lijun Zhu
items.summary: The anomalous Hall voltage of magnetic heterostructures plays a key role via the interplay with a variety of spintronic effects. Under a given electric field (E), the anomalous Hall voltage of a magnetic layer should remain unaffected by adjacent layers unless the latter could modify or contribute to the anomalous Hall conductivity. In this Letter, we report the observation, universality, mechanism, and impacts of the dramatic scaling of the apparent anomalous Hall voltage per electric field (VAH/E) of magnetic heterostructures with the thickness and resistivity of the nonmagnetic conducting layers by combining transport experiments, analytical derivation, and finite-element analyses. We identify that the scaling arises simply from the misreading of the invariant internal anomalous Hall voltage due to the series-resistor effect of the magnetic and nonmagnetic layers within the magnetic heterostructures. The scaling remains strong regardless of the strengths of the spin–orbit torques and spin and orbital Hall conductivities of the normal metals, suggesting that interfacial angular momentum transport plays a minimal role in the anomalous Hall effect. We also show that the harmonic Hall voltage analyses of magnetic heterostructures remain robust against the considerable underestimation of the anomalous Hall voltage and other transverse voltages due to the series-resistor effect. These findings provide crucial information for understanding a variety of spintronic experiments involving the anomalous Hall and other transverse voltages.

items.title: Emergent Interfacial Magnetism in Epitaxial RuO2
authors: Yudi Yang, Zhuang Qian, Shi Liu and Congjun Wu
items.summary: The magnetic ground state of the altermagnet candidate RuO2 remains controversial, with magnetic signatures observed mainly in epitaxial films. Here we show, using first-principles calculations, that magnetism in epitaxial RuO2 can emerge as an interfacial boundary phase at TiO2/RuO2 interfaces. While TiO2-induced epitaxial strain alone does not make (001)-oriented RuO2 magnetic, explicit TiO2/RuO2 interfaces stabilize sizable Ru moments confined to the first few Ru layers. Charge-density and orbital-resolved analyses reveal interfacial electronic reconstruction, and substrate doping provides a route to tune the induced moments. In symmetric TiO2/RuO2/TiO2 heterostructures, the two magnetic interfaces couple through the metallic RuO2 spacer, producing a thickness-dependent alternation between weak-ferromagnetic and compensated altermagnetic states for even RuO2 thicknesses. authors: Mengru Jiang, 梦茹 江, Zhaoyao Pan, 赵耀 潘, Jiaqi Quan, 家琪 权, Qiming Hu, 琦明 胡, Yadong Xu and 亚东 徐
items.summary: Gradient metasurfaces provide a powerful platform for wavefront and dynamic beam steering of electromagnetic and acoustic waves by introducing the phase-gradient degree of freedom, but they still suffer from narrow steering angles and low efficiency due to inherent dispersion. Here, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a dispersionless gradient metasurface approach that offers a practical yet powerful route to wide-angle, near-perfect beam steering, overcoming the longstanding trade-off between bandwidth and efficiency in metasurface design. As a proof of concept, we design and fabricate an acoustic metasurface operating at 3430 Hz, which exhibits near-perfect anomalous refraction with an efficiency exceeding 85% over an unprecedented bandwidth of 44.4% (2800–4400 Hz). This performance enables continuous frequency-driven beam steering from 46.5° to 15.8°, covering a 30.7° field of view. Serving as a critical transition between anomalous and normal dispersion, the concept of dispersionless gradient metasurfaces provides a criterion for evaluating the bandwidth limitations of various dispersive counterparts, and establishes a new paradigm for high-performance, frequency-driven dynamic wavefront manipulation.

items.title: Evidence of Polarons and Their Ultrafast Optical Undressing in a Topological Semimetal
authors: Lei Hou, Yunkun Yang, Heming Xia, Jun Yin, Pengcheng Ji, Yujun Zhang, Wen Xu, Faxian Xiu, and Lan Ding
items.summary: Abstract Polarons, formed by coupling electrons with lattice vibrations, are of intense interest in topological semimetals owing to their crucial role in dictating high-speed topological optoelectronics. However, polarons in topological semimetals have thus far been exclusively observed as light-induced transient quasiparticles, leaving equilibrium polarons and their ultrafast dynamics elusive. Here, using time-resolved magneto-terahertz spectroscopy, we demonstrate the ultrafast optical undressing of polarons in a Cd 3 As 2 thin film. In equilibrium, a magnetic-field-induced spectral splitting near the 1.22-terahertz phonon mode reveals an 87% enhancement of the carrier effective mass due to the polaron effect. Upon photoexcitation, the enhanced carrier effective mass collapses within 5 ps, reflecting the transient undressing of this pre-existing polaronic state. Notably, this anomalous suppression contrasts sharply with prior studies where optical excitation exclusively triggers polaron formation in topological semimetals. This study provides deep insights into the ultrafast magneto-optical dynamics of pre-existing polarons, advancing the design of high-performance topological devices.

items.title: Light-Triggered Self-Growth of 3D Photonic Structures with Vertical Helical-Pitch Gradients Engineering
authors: Jiemin Qiu, Jie Li, and Rui Xiong
items.summary: Abstract Natural structural colors often emerge from interactions between chiral lattices and three-dimensional (3D) microstructures, yet integrating surface topography with structural order in artificial photonic materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a light-driven self-growth strategy for programmable 3D photonic structures by engineering through-thickness gradients in a preassembled chiral nematic cellulose scaffold. Confined UV photopolymerization drives localized reactions and directional mass transport, creating coupled gradients in cross-linking density, polymer concentration, and helical pitch. These gradients enable continuous structural-color tuning from blue to red, while differential swelling-induced buckling produces patterned protrusions with programmable heights. The resulting interpenetrating network provides structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Combined with photomask lithography, this approach yields spatially resolved multicolor architectures featuring programmable 3D topographies, angle-dependent optical responses, and self-cleaning properties. It further enables four-channel optical encryption integrating polarization, multipeak reflection, 3D topography, and photoluminescence, demonstrating gradient engineering as a versatile route to advanced multifunctional bioinspired photonic material design.

items.title: Quantifying and Managing the Structural Lifetimes of Nanocrystalline Model Catalysts in CO
authors: Lei Ying, Qingli Tang, Beien Zhu, and Yi Gao
items.summary: Abstract Dynamic restructuring of metal nanocrystals (MNCs) in reactive gas atmospheres challenges the static paradigm of shape-controlled model catalysis. Quantifying their structural lifetimes under operating conditions is essential, yet predicting atomistic kinetics over macroscopic time scales remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we transform unpredictable structural lifetimes into a manageable variable using an improved environmental kinetic Monte Carlo (iEKMC) method. It overcomes traditional time scale limits and predicts Pt NC reshaping kinetics across macroscopic time domains under CO atmospheres. By resolving the combined effects of initial morphology, particle size, and temperature, we establish a quantitative framework that determines the reshaping time of MNCs under reaction conditions, showing consistency with benchmarking experiments. We demonstrate that selected combinations of particle size and reaction conditions can effectively mitigate restructuring, preserving predesigned MNC morphologies over day-scale observation windows. This work evaluates and manages operando shape stability in a predictive strategy, restoring the core validity of shape-controlled model catalysis.

items.title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene
authors: Yingnan Liu, Yan Liu, Renyu Duan, Menghui Wang, Meiling Xu, Hanyu Liu, and Shoutao Zhang
items.summary: Abstract Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron–phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of ∼100–113 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high- T c boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane σ-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B–B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s – p z -bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s – p z bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high- T c superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.

items.title: Strategy and Mechanism of Boosting Ion Penetration in Organic Electrochemical Transistors
authors: Dianjue Liu, Zhongyou Lu, Mengfu Chen, Lizhen Huang, and Lifeng Chi
items.summary: Abstract Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic devices because of their unique ionic–electronic coupling. The key to unlocking high-performance operations lies in achieving rapid and efficient bulk doping, yet this remains critically hampered by limited ion accessibility, particularly within the hydrophobic bulk of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs). This mini-review highlights recent molecular and processing engineering strategies to enhance ion penetration and ion–electron coupling in OECT channels. Molecular-level tuning, such as side-chain and backbone modulation, in addition to processing approaches, including the use of additives, dopants, cross-linked networks, solvent engineering, patterned transport architectures, and interface microstructure control, are discussed. Throughout, we place special emphasis on elucidating the complex relationships between molecular structure, processing-derived morphology, interfacial environments, and ion–transport dynamics, complemented by advanced characterization approaches that probe ion transport and its coupling with hydration and structural evolution. This holistic understanding is pivotal for rational performance optimization. Finally, we highlight emerging frontiers in advanced characterization, multiscale simulation, and data-driven design, which are expected to expedite the discovery of high-performance OMIECs and OECTs with balanced and enhanced mixed transport properties.

items.title: Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework-Confined Carbon Dots toward Efficient Red Room-Temperature Phosphorescence via Resonance Energy Transfer
authors: Zhenti Xu, Wenjie Xu, Jiurong Li, Wenxuan Sun, and Xiao Gong
items.summary: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials are promising for information encryption and anticounterfeiting. However, realizing long-wavelength RTP of carbon dots (CDs) is challenging owing to unstable triplet states and strong nonradiative decay. Herein, we construct a hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) through molecular self-assembly and realize the in situ generation of CDs within the HOF matrix. By further incorporating Rhodamine B (RhB) into the HOF, a donor–acceptor resonance energy transfer (RET) system is established, enabling efficient red RTP emission. In this system, the HOF matrix provides a confined environment for the CDs and RhB. Meanwhile, the hydrogen-bonded network restricts excited-state molecular motions and suppresses nonradiative relaxation. The optimized CDs-RhB@HOF composite exhibits outstanding red phosphorescence centered at 600 nm, achieving a high PLQY of 34.20% (versus 0.71% for CDs@HOF) and a prolonged lifetime of 458 ms. The composite material has been successfully applied to multilevel anticounterfeiting encryption.

items.title: Nonlinear Hall Effect in a Semiconductor Heterostructure with Rashba and Dresselhaus Effects
authors: Jeong Ung Ahn, Junyeong Choi, Minseong Kwon, Won-Young Choi, Ki Hyuk Han, Cheol Jun Kim, Chaun Jang, Dong-Soo Han, OukJae Lee, Byoung-Chul Min, Kyoung-Whan Kim, and Hyun Cheol Koo
items.summary: Abstract We report a nonlinear Hall effect in a high-mobility InAs quantum-well two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) with coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus spin–orbit interactions. Under zero magnetic field, a second-harmonic transverse electric field emerges that scales quadratically with current density and is significantly larger than the second-harmonic longitudinal response. Angle-dependent measurements reveal a pronounced 2-fold anisotropy that follows the combined spin–orbit field. This 2-fold symmetry reflects the anisotropic spin–orbit field generated by coexisting Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions rather than crystal symmetry. The normalized signal reaches ∼10 –9 V –1 m and persists up to room temperature. Conductivity scaling shows a quadratic dependence consistent with skew-scattering-dominated transport. These results establish conventional semiconductor 2DEGs as a promising platform for spin-orbit-driven nonlinear transport and rectification functionalities.

items.title: Minerals Modulate Lithium Ion Sieve for Efficient Lithium Extraction
authors: Cheng Zhang, Runqin Gao, Kun Yu, Qian Wang, Xiongbo Dong, and Huaming Yang
items.summary: Abstract Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is vital for lithium-resource supply. Nevertheless, practical application of titanium-based H 2 TiO 3 (HTO) ion sieves is limited by insufficient adsorption performance. Herein, a high-performance HTO adsorbent (HTO-VMT) was fabricated using vermiculite to regulate the spatial coordination environment and surface hydrophilicity of HTO. Theoretical calculations and experimental analysis reveal that vermiculite, as a Si source and support for HTO, enables interfacial Si migration through isovalent substitution of Ti atoms, leading to atomic-level integration into the HTO crystal lattice. The Si substitution results in an upward shift of the p-band center of O of HTO, which enhanced hybridizations between Li 2s and O 2p orbitals, thus accelerating lithium adsorption rates in the surface diffusion phase. Thanks to an optimal coordination structure and surface hydrophilicity, HTO-VMT exhibits exceptional lithium extraction performance, surpassing state-of-the-art counterparts. This work provides design insights for Li-selective adsorbents via mineral-mediated atomic-scale coordination modulation.

items.title: Finite-Depth Interfacial Coupling in Metal/Topological Insulator van der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Yin-Song Liao, Hsin-Hsien Chan, Ruei-Yu Wang, Han-Wei Tsai, Hsun-Ting Hsieh, Cheng-Maw Cheng, Jyh-Pin Chou, and Meng-Kai Lin
items.summary: Abstract Metal/topological insulator van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures offer a platform for engineering emergent quantum states beyond isolated layers. While proximity effects in covalently bonded systems are well studied, coupling depth across vdW interfaces remains unclear. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we investigate the thickness dependence of TiTe 2 /Bi 2 Te 3 electronic states. Despite nominally weak vdW bonding, the buried interface induces emergent bands and splitting near a band crossing, consistent with hybridization. Interface-induced features persist in the bilayer, while band evolution nearly saturates in thicker films. Even at four layers, the electronic structure does not simply recover to the intrinsic TiTe 2 limit, consistent with finite-depth coupling that substantially reshapes the overlayer bands. Charge redistribution and a moiré-modulated interfacial potential contribute to this reconstruction. Finite-depth coupling may be a hallmark of strongly coupled vdW heterostructures and guide topological and quantum electronic device design.

items.title: Numerical study on fluctuation characteristics of millimeter-wave rain attenuation
authors: Pengcheng Zhao, 朋程 赵, Lixin Guo and 立新 郭
items.summary: The application of millimeter waves constitutes a key component of the fifth generation (5G) and beyond wireless technologies, yet rainy weather can impose adverse impacts on wireless channels. In this paper, the dielectric mixture model with full consideration of the influence of rainfall drop size distribution (DSD) is used to predict the specific attenuation of millimeter waves. The fluctuation characteristics of rain attenuation are characterized by an empirical lognormal distribution formula. Simulation results show that the specific attenuation predicted by the dielectric mixture model is close to the measured average when the traditional Weibull DSD is applied to the prediction of two specific wireless links. Moreover, the distribution of simulated specific attenuation under a fixed rainfall rate exhibits good agreement with the measured data. The fluctuation characteristics of rain attenuation are explained by adjusting the parameters of the Weibull DSD.

items.title: Unveiling dynamic mechanism of crystallization for the uranium peroxide
authors: Wei Gong, 伟 龚, Zehui Zhang, 泽辉 张, Yongdong Xu, 永东 徐, Naizhe Zhang, 乃哲 张, Xiaojuan Liu, 晓娟 刘, Yiming Gao, 一鸣 高, Minghong Wu, 明红 吴, Guosheng Shi and 国升 石
items.summary: As a critical fuel of nuclear energy, uranium peroxide precipitation and conversion represent critical steps in uranium extraction processes, directly determining the purity and recovery efficiency of the final product. However, the dynamic mechanism of uranium peroxide precipitation and conversion remains unclear. Here, we investigated the crystallization kinetics of metal peroxides, establishing empirical equations between crystallization rate and solution supersaturation under different metal concentration ranges. Combining the experimental observations with theoretical calculations, we showed that at the lower metal concentration the crystal growth dominates the crystallization process, while at the higher concentration range nucleation becomes the dominant process. Further, mathematical models were developed to correlate crystallization rate with solution composition and operating parameters. Our findings provide fundamental insights to support the development of more efficient and scalable precipitation processes, addressing key challenges in uranium purification and recovery.

items.title: Intrinsic electron–hole separation and tunable valley polarization in strain-engineered MXene Cr2COCl
authors: Xiaoyang He, 小杨 贺, Chen Chen, 晨 陈, Chuye Quan, 楚烨 全, Shilei Ji, 石磊 季, Jianping Yang, 建平 杨, Xing’ao Li and 兴鳌 李
items.summary: Valleytronics, as an emerging electronic degree of freedom, holds significant potential in low-power devices. However, achieving valley polarization and efficient electron–hole separation remains a challenge. Through first-principles calculations, this study proposes the two-dimensional MXene material Cr2COCl as an ideal platform for valleytronics. The results indicate that Cr2COCl is a ferromagnetic semiconductor with significant valley polarization properties. Its unique layer-resolved orbital contributions enable intrinsic electron–hole separation, thereby effectively suppressing carrier recombination. Biaxial strain linearly modulates valley splitting and Berry curvature, enabling reversible control of the anomalous valley Hall effect. When tensile strain is applied, the system undergoes a topological phase transition, producing a nonzero Chern number (C = 1) and chiral edge states. These findings confirm that Cr2COCl can be used to regulate carriers, adjust valley polarization, and generate topological states through strain engineering, providing a theoretical basis for designing high-performance, low-power valleytronic devices.

items.title: Effects of free surface on primary radiation damage in α-Fe induced by different ion irradiations: A molecular dynamics study
authors: Lin Jiang, 林 江, Teng Kang, 腾 康, Min Li, 敏 李, Baoqin Fu, 宝勤 付, Jiechao Cui, 节超 崔, Qing Hou and 氢 侯
items.summary: Ion irradiation serves as a critical tool for investigating material response to radiation-induced damage. This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to systematically investigate surface damage in α-Fe under Ar, Fe, and Au ion irradiation, with cascade damage in bulk Fe included for comparative analysis. The simulation results demonstrate that the presence of a free surface significantly enhances vacancy production for all three ion species compared to bulk cascades, with the severity of surface damage following the order of Au > Fe > Ar. This trend is primarily driven by ion-specific penetration depths. Further analysis reveals that equivalent penetration depth methods — including SRIM-predicted energies and reduced incident energies — fail to ensure consistent damage outcomes across ion species. These findings highlight that ion irradiation damage is governed by a coupled mechanism involving both energy transfer processes within the cascade and the modulating influence of the free surface, with ion species playing a pivotal role in determining the resulting microstructural evolution.

items.title: CMOS-compatible ferroelectric artificial dendrite for spatiotemporal integration
authors: Sen Liu, 森 刘, Zi-Hao Hou, 子浩 侯, Peng Yang, 彭 杨, Lei Liu, 磊 刘, Xu Guo, 旭 郭, Nan Li, 楠 李, Zhi-Wei Li, 智炜 李, Yi Sun, 毅 孙, Qing-Jiang Li and 清江 李
items.summary: In biological neural systems, dendrites play an essential role in spatiotemporal information processing, which enables the brain to manage complex tasks with minimal energy. In this study, for the first time, we propose a CMOS-compatible dual-gate ferroelectric thin film transistor (FeTFT) for emulating spatiotemporal information processing in biological dendrites. Owing to the utilization of CMOS-compatible materials and fabrication processes, the FeTFT exhibits exceptional retention characteristics (>106 s) and endurance characteristics (>1012). The following experimental results show that the dendritic spatial and temporal integration can be replicated in the FeTFT device with varying pulse sequences. These superior characteristics, combined with its unique spatiotemporal processing capability, position this novel device as a highly promising candidate for advanced large-scale neuromorphic computing systems, particularly in applications requiring complex signal integration and parallel processing.

items.title: Delay-independent stability of switched fractional nonlinear delayed systems
authors: Xianbo Huang, 贤波 黄, Song Liu, 松 刘, Denghao Pang and 登浩 庞
items.summary: This paper investigates the stability of switched fractional nonlinear delayed systems, in which all subsystems may be unstable. By employing a state-dependent switching strategy, the fractional Razumikhin technique, and the common Lyapunov function approach, a framework for stability analysis is developed, and several delay-independent conditions for uniform asymptotic stability are presented. The proposed method addresses challenges arising from unstable modes, time delays, and fractional derivatives. The obtained results further demonstrate that stability will still be achieved even when all subsystems are unstable. Finally, a practical circuit switching example is provided to illustrate the application of the theoretical conclusions.

items.title: Witnessing quantum steering and nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence via the quantum steering ellipsoid
authors: Huan Yang, 欢 杨, Ling-Ling Xing, 玲玲 邢, Zong Xu, 棕 许, Gang Zhang and 刚 张
items.summary: An arbitrary bipartite state can be visually characterized through a quantum steering ellipsoid (QSE), with different nonclassical correlations visually revealed via the geometric traits of the QSE. Here, we characterize the QSE of bipartite Bell diagonal states subject to bit flip (BF), depolarizing (DP), and phase damping (PD) channels and evaluate the effect of various noise channels on the QSE. Using the nonlinear asymmetric quantum steering criterion (NAC), linear asymmetric quantum steering criterion (LAC), quantum steering criterion from the entropic uncertainty relation (SCEUR), and the QSE shape, we detect quantum steering and the nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence (NAQC) in the system under these noise channels. It turns out that noise channels can significantly deform the shape of the QSE; one can effectively capture quantum steering and the NAQC via the QSE. Among the NAC, LAC, and SCEUR, the LAC is the most promising avenue for detecting quantum steering under the DP and PD channels, while NAC best detects it under BF channels. Notably, the QSE’s shape reveals the relative effectiveness of these criteria in detecting quantum steering. Moreover, based on the l1 norm of coherence, NAQC occurs under the BF, DP, and PD channels when the sum of the QSE’s three semiaxis lengths exceeds .

items.title: Emergent interweaved CDW unoccupied states in hole-doping LaTe2 with element substitution
authors: Shuya Xing, 淑雅 邢, Hongyu Liu, 宏宇 刘, Xu Chen, 旭 陈, Zhenkai Xie, 圳楷 谢, Zhongxu Wei, 忠旭 魏, Shifeng Zhao, 世峰 赵, Wenping Zhou, 文平 周, Xinqi Li, 新奇 李, Zhihai Cheng and 志海 程
items.summary: Multiple charge density wave (CDW)-ordered layered rare-earth tellurides have increasingly emerged as a research hotspot owing to their unconventional CDW formation, high transition temperatures, and confirmed existence of axial Higgs modes. Recently, interweaved CDWs in LaTe2 and its element-substituted phase LaTe2−xSbx have been investigated through TEM and ARPES measurements, revealing their distinct origins. Nevertheless, several complex diffraction features observed in TEM patterns remain unexplained. In this work, we carried out scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) on LaTe1.6Sb0.4 crystals at 9 K. Three interweaved CDW wave vectors, q1 = 8/11a*, q2 = 5/11a* and q3 = 3/11a*, were observed, which are induced by hole doping in unoccupied states. The q1 and q3 vectors are theoretically verified to be nesting vectors connecting px and py bands. Furthermore, satellite spots relative to the main Bragg spots, corresponding to an 11-a superlattice, have also been detected. Our findings provide critical insights into further exploring the origin of interweaved CDWs in hole- and electron-doped materials.

items.title: Unconventional chiral d-wave superconductivity in the t–J–U model on a honeycomb lattice
authors: Lianjun Zou, 濂军 邹, Feng Xu and 峰 徐
items.summary: We investigate chiral d-wave superconductivity in the honeycomb-lattice t–J–U model within renormalized mean-field theory (RMFT). By incorporating Gutzwiller renormalization factors, we treat the effects of strong correlations and the suppression of double occupancy self-consistently. For the nearest-neighbor chiral d + id-wave pairing state on the honeycomb lattice, we analyze the evolution of the pairing amplitude, the quasiparticle spectrum, and the superfluid weight as functions of doping concentration, local Coulomb repulsion (U), and antiferromagnetic exchange interaction (J). The pairing amplitude exhibits a dome-like doping dependence. As U increases, the dome broadens and shifts toward higher hole concentrations due to the renormalization of the effective kinetic energy. We further determine the critical value of the exchange interaction required to obtain a self-consistent pairing solution and show that strong correlations reduce this threshold over a wide doping range. Finally, using the calculated superfluid weight, we estimate the phase-ordering temperature scale associated with the self-consistent chiral d-wave solution. Our results clarify how correlation effects influence chiral d-wave pairing and the superfluid weight in honeycomb-lattice systems.

items.title: Cross-scale lattice distortions and vibration spectra in Bi2Se3 revealed by ultrafast transmission electron microscopy
authors: Xiao-Tian Wang, 骁天 王, Wenli Gao, 文莉 高, Yongzhao Zhang, 永朝 张, Yanqing Tong, 彦青 佟, Junxi Tong, 俊淅 童, Jun Li, 俊 李, Huanfang Tian, 焕芳 田, Huaixin Yang, 槐馨 杨, Shuaishuai Sun, 帅帅 孙, Jianqi Li and 建奇 李
items.summary: Layered topological insulators such as Bi2Se3 exhibit rich phonon dynamics, which are crucial for understanding their thermal transport mechanisms and electronic properties. In this work, we investigate the multiscale nonequilibrium lattice dynamics in Bi2Se3 thin films using ultrafast transmission electron microscopy (UTEM). By exploiting the complementarity between real-space ultrafast electron microscopy (UEM) and ultrafast electron diffraction (UED), we show that the characteristic frequencies of the lattice dynamics are consistent in real and reciprocal space. This cross-validation supports the interpretation that the transient anti-phase oscillation of Friedel diffraction pairs originates from reciprocal-space geometric evolution induced by the breathing mode: under large-angle tilting, reciprocal rods with nonzero out-of-plane Miller indices undergo periodic stretching and displacement along the c* axis, thereby asymmetrically changing their intersections with the Ewald sphere. This process corresponds directly to the coherent motion of lattice bend contours observed in real space. The study further reveals that phonon propagation exhibits pronounced scale dependence. On the picosecond timescale, the dynamics are dominated by a longitudinal standing-wave breathing mode confined by the film thickness, with the oscillation frequency following an inverse dependence on film thickness. Under the [001] zone-axis condition, defect-mediated in-plane traveling waves propagating at the speed of sound are observed. Furthermore, on the nanosecond timescale, the suspended thin film exhibits mechanical resonance with a high quality factor, accompanied by a rich spectrum of higher-order harmonics. These findings provide direct visual evidence for the multilevel dynamical responses of coherent phonons under the same pump excitation, manifesting across different timescales and boundary conditions, from the gigahertz (GHz) to megahertz (MHz) regime, highlighting the potential of Bi2Se3 for high-frequency nanomechanical applications.

items.title: Atomic Lift-Off of Wafer-Scale Single-Crystalline Gold Membranes Enables Buried-Interface Epitaxy for Flexible Oxide Electronics
authors: Yongbin Sun, Hanwen Chi, Ziyue Shen, Kaixin Wang, Fan Zhang, Ni Tu, Tianhao Yang, Wenzhe Niu, Zhizhen Ye, Liping Zhu, and Jie Jiang
items.summary: Abstract Flexible oxide electronics require inorganic semiconductors that maintain high-performance under bending, yet scalable approaches to wafer-scale single-crystalline (SC) oxide films and, critically, atomically sharp metal/oxide contacts remain limited. Here, we introduce a buried-interface epitaxy strategy based on atomic lift-off of epitaxial metal films to create atomically defined SC metal/oxide heterostructures in flexible architectures. We fabricate 2-in. freestanding SC Au(111) membranes and employ film-flipping to expose the originally buried Au/Si epitaxial interface as an intrinsically atomically flat growth surface. This converts conventional surface deposition into interface deposition, enabling wafer-scale epitaxial Cu 2 O(111)/Au with a flat interface. The interface-deposited flexible Cu 2 O exhibits nearly 2-fold higher carrier mobility and photocurrent, while maintaining stable transport under bending. Flexible Cu 2 O photocathodes further exhibit 1.6 times higher full-angle light harvesting and 5.6 times higher photocurrent-to-mass metrics compared with rigid counterparts. This work establishes freestanding SC metals as transferable epitaxial templates for flexible oxide electronics and energy devices.
